Sorry Clare, you are amazing but it is clear that you  are struggling to run a successful business.

Would I recommend MP Motorsportz for an MOT? Absolutely not.

I originally booked my car into VAG Tune Services to investigate an issue, and the vehicle was then taken to MP Motorsportz for the MOT. I was later informed that the car had failed because the CV boot was supposedly “missing,” and I was quoted around £450 to fix the issue.

As someone who knows my vehicle well, I was very surprised by this diagnosis and decided to seek second opinions. Two independent mechanics both confirmed that the CV boot was present and in good condition, and that the repair quoted was unnecessary.

As a young woman, I found this situation particularly concerning. It felt as though assumptions may have been made about my knowledge, and that I was being asked to pay for work that did not need to be carried out. This was extremely frustrating and has seriously undermined my trust.

I would strongly advise others to double-check unexpected repair findings and consider getting a second opinion before agreeing to costly work.

Based on my experience, I will not be returning and would not recommend using this service for an MOT.

We paid for new electrics and plumbing, but what we received was substandard work that does not meet British Standards. The electrical certificate provided does not reflect the actual work completed, which is deeply concerning.
The quality of workmanship throughout our home is unacceptable. Doors, hinges, and frames have all been damaged or poorly fitted. Bathrooms are leaking, floors are unstable, tiles are broken, and paving in both the front and back garden was lifted and not properly reinstated. There are even exposed wires, posing a serious safety risk.
Communication has also been extremely difficult. When challenged, the director becomes defensive, often shifting blame onto us or making excuses. We also experienced items going missing during the project, which we were told had been “thrown away” by staff.
Additionally, the subcontractors and suppliers associated with this company (including window fitters and roofers) have been equally unreliable, taking payment and failing to address issues or respond to concerns.
What was meant to be a facility for my ill father has turned into a source of immense stress and financial strain for our entire family. We are now forced to redo much of the work at additional cost.
I strongly advise others to avoid this company. Based on our experience, hiring them will likely lead to poor workmanship, ongoing issues, and significant emotional and financial hardship.

one_star_reviews.text:
A couple of years ago I went to test drive a Nissan 370Z here that was up for around £17k. The owner was there and said his son would assist me.

The first thing I got asked was whether I knew much about the car. Honestly, apart from getting lifts in one a couple of times with a work colleague, I didn’t — which is exactly why I expected the salesman to actually tell me a bit about it. Instead I pretty much just got “ok”.

Then came the test drive… which was basically up to the roundabout and straight back. Maybe 5–6 minutes total. For a £17k sports car. Easily the shortest and least informative test drive I’ve ever had.

I wasn’t massively sold on the 370Z, but I spotted a BMW Z4 there and asked if I could test that instead. I was told it was blocked in at the back and they’d have to move cars around, so they wouldn’t let me drive it — only sit in it. Ironically, sitting in that Z4 is what made me decide that’s actually the car I wanted. Just not from here.

A few months later I ended up buying a stunning Z4 35i with red seats elsewhere. Funny enough, this dealership actually had a black one at the time for similar money which looked amazing as well, but after the experience I had no interest in dealing with them further.

The owner’s reply honestly says everything. Instead of just accepting the experience was poor, it comes across incredibly defensive and arrogant — almost like customers are an inconvenience rather than the entire reason the business exists.

The whole “why leave a review 2 years later?” comment is a strange point to focus on. I came across the dealership again recently while looking at cars and noticed there were already multiple 1-star reviews in the last 9 months describing very similar issues with attitude and customer service. It just reminded me of my own experience and confirmed it clearly wasn’t an isolated bad day.

Time passing doesn’t suddenly make poor customer service good.

And the explanation about the unit being so full they couldn’t get another car out? That genuinely made me laugh. If the place is permanently jammed with stock and customers can barely test drive cars properly, maybe that’s part of the problem. Usually dealerships make an effort to actually sell cars and create a good experience, especially when someone is potentially spending £17k–£20k.

Reading other replies on here shows the same pattern too — blaming customers, getting defensive, refusing to take ownership, and acting like basic expectations are unreasonable. If someone drives 115 miles to view a car, making a simple phone call if it sells is just common courtesy.

Overall the whole experience felt dismissive, uninterested and honestly like they were doing me a favour by even letting me look at the cars.

I purchased a SEAT Leon Cupra 290 2016 from Kash who also owns Berkshire van centre Limited in February 2023. The sale was done as a private deal, separate from his business Berkshire Van Centre Limited.

At the same time, I part-exchanged my Volkswagen Polo. During the valuation, I was told my Polo was not worth much more than what I was being offered. I accepted this. However, within a few days, I saw the same Polo listed on AutoTrader for roughly double the price I was given, despite it having no issues at the time of trade-in. So he just basically lied to my face and was dishonest.

The Cupra cost me £13,995. On inspection it initially seemed fine, so I proceeded with the purchase. However, within the following days turning into weeks, serious issues started to appear.

I began noticing aggressive engine vibration. Even from the 2nd day of me having the car it was doing this but I didn’t think anything of this until it started getting a lot worse. Kash definitely knew about this when he sold this car to me but he hid it quite well. Not long after, an inlet manifold leak was discovered, which became worse when the car was left idling. This continued to escalate over the following weeks until the engine eventually shut down completely while driving. I had to take the car to Extreme Motors in Mitcham for repairs, which cost me over £1,000 out of my own pocket.

In addition to engine issues, all four wheels were in extremely poor condition. One alloy was severely cracked and had previously been spot welded. This caused ongoing tyre problems on the front driver-side wheel that persisted for over 3 years of ownership until I eventually sold the car in 2026.

The car also had a persistent damper/suspension warning light from the day I bought it. I was told this was due to the suspension being replaced and that it was a known issue for this model. However, later inspection showed that incorrect aftermarket suspension had been fitted, and wiring had been cut/altered, meaning the adaptive suspension system the car was designed to use was not functioning properly at all.
On top of this, I was told the issue was “normal” for the car, which later turned out not to be the case.

Over time I spent thousands of pounds dealing with the issues this car had, none of which were disclosed properly at the point of sale.

After purchasing the car, there was no meaningful follow-up or support. Any communication I had felt dismissive, and I still have WhatsApp voice notes from around the time of the sale that reflect this. I was also met with rudeness when asking for basic documentation to be completed which was the logbook and paperwork.
The only reason I didn’t raise this earlier is because it became clear nothing would be done about it after the sale, so I’ve simply chosen to leave an honest review now.

I have since sold the SEAT Leon cupra recently after the work that had to be done on it and moved on to a 2021 BMW M340i xDrive purchased directly from an BMW approved dealership, and the difference in transparency and condition has been night and day.

Based on my experience, I would strongly avoid making a purchase. I will also be sharing this review so others are fully aware of my experience before making any decisions.

And just to let you know “kash” you still watch my WhatsApp status stories to this day and haven’t said a word which is very unusual. Just know that I’ll be sharing this with people I know and make sure it gets spread around because at the end of the day, even though you have a van business with positive reviews. You are a big conman. You take advantage of private sales on the side of your van business because you know you can take advantage of people.

I can also providing clear supporting evidence for my review including video/photographs of the incorrect suspension work, damaged rims, Xtreme Motors paperwork detailing the job that was meant to be completed, and In addition, I am including the WhatsApp voice note received after the sale which was rude and dismissive.

My father stayed at Oakleaf for just a few days, and unfortunately our experience raised serious concerns about the standard of care he received.

On the Friday, I noticed he seemed unusually cold and mentioned this to a staff member. I was reassured that it was “nothing to worry about” and told that feeling cold was common. However, in hindsight, this may have been an early sign that something was wrong.

In the early hours of Sunday morning, my father became unwell and was taken to hospital. What was particularly distressing is that our family was not informed until several hours after he had already been admitted. We were told he had suffered another stroke. When I later raised this with the manager, explaining that we should have been contacted immediately in such a serious situation, I was told that “some family members don’t like to be called at night.” I found this response deeply concerning—when a loved one is seriously ill, being informed promptly should never be optional.

When we arrived at the hospital, we were relieved to learn that he had not suffered a stroke but had pneumonia. However, the misinformation and delay in communication caused significant and unnecessary distress to our family.

There were also worrying issues with his day-to-day care. On his first morning, he was given two breakfasts, suggesting a lack of coordination or record-keeping. Additionally, when staff were repositioning him in bed, they did not appear to know how to support him properly following his stroke. I had to intervene and explain how his affected side should be positioned and elevated.

The environment itself was also quite noisy, which may not be suitable for patients who need rest and recovery.

Based on our experience, I would strongly advise anyone considering Oakleaf to visit in advance, ask detailed questions, and ensure that the level of care meets your expectations. Our experience was upsetting, and I would not want other families to go through the same.

BVRLA membership does not provide customers with the "reassurance that the company they are dealing with adheres to the highest standards of professionalism and fairness." Instead of improving or "reinforcing industry standards and regulatory compliance," the BVRLA allows these practices to persist, enabling customers to be charged for various fees unrelated to the car rental itself.

One would expect the BVRLA to protect its members and, by extension, customers, from these non-car rental-related fees imposed by external parties. However, the pattern is clear: decades of inaction, as their focus has never truly been on the car rental or hire industry.

It’s time to raise awareness and steer clear of car rental companies that support such practices. We are committed to continuously exposing these issues on social media and in front of policymakers.

As a result, I have now started legal proceedings to recover the money.
Action Fraud Ref: NFRC231206352995

Avoid at all COSTS!

1. Initial Agreement and Payment:
- Found the property on SpareRooms and agreed to rent it after being promised all maintenance would be completed before moving in on 5th October 2023.
- Paid a holding deposit on 29th September 2023 and agreed to an increased rent with a 3-month break-in period.

2. Delay in Moving In:
- Keys were not received until 17th October 2023, three weeks after the promised date.
- Maintenance works (changing the sofa, repairing intercom, changing blinds) were not done as agreed.

3. Payment Issues:
- Paid £15,000 on 6th October 2023 (3 months rent + security deposit).
- Discovered unpaid electricity bills for the past three months and couldn't transfer the bill to our name due to the contract not being signed by Idasons Ltd.

4. Contract and Management Problems:
- DIJ Real Estate uses "let only" contracts, requiring tenants to deal with the landlord or managing agent (Idasons Ltd) after paying.
- Idasons Ltd threatened us in November, claiming non-receipt of full payment from DIJ Real Estate despite our full payment.

5. Maintenance Neglect:
- Multiple calls to DIJ Real Estate and Idasons Ltd were made, but no maintenance work was completed.

6. Deposit Issues:
- Security deposit was not protected in any TDS scheme, a breach of contract.
- Previous tenants also did not get their security deposits back and filed claims with legal firms like Phoenix Solicitors.

7. NDA and Deposit Return:
- Duane from DIJ Real Estate promised to return the deposit if we deleted all reviews and signed an NDA.
- Received the deposit back on 8th July 2024 after vacating the flat on 12th January 2024, following hundreds of emails and signing the NDA.

8. Financial Warning:
- Idasons Ltd , DIJ Real Estate, DIJ Investments are all bankrupt according to government financial statements.

Additional Facts:
- Returned deposit was only received after extensive follow-up and legal pressure.

I purchased an electric wheelchair from Better Mobility. I have a neuromuscular condition, spinal fusion, and am non-ambulant. In my experience, I was provided with unsuitable seating without a full specialist seating assessment by the director.

I had always previously used a solid supportive backrest with hip support, however I was supplied with a canvas backrest and no pelvic/hip support. Within weeks of receiving the chair, I began experiencing sensory changes and worsening physical issues. Since then, I have had multiple assessments through private specialists and the NHS, including a lengthy assessment involving a physiotherapist and seating specialists, and I have consistently been advised that this type of seating would not usually be recommended for someone with my level of spinal complexity.

The health impact on me has been severe and life-changing. I now live with chronic pain, inflammation, reduced independence, and ongoing medical treatment. From my perspective, this situation may have been avoidable with a proper specialist assessment at the time.

I also experienced other issues during my time dealing with the company, including concerns regarding speed settings on my wheelchair and communication around equipment assessments.

I appreciate that others may have different experiences, but personally I would strongly encourage anyone with complex seating or spinal needs to seek a full assessment through experienced NHS or specialist seating professionals before purchasing a wheelchair setup.

Update: I previously removed an earlier response after concerns about private information being shared publicly. I maintain that this review reflects my honest personal experience and the significant impact the seating provided had on my health and quality of life.

I tried to open an account with them as I thought this would be an easy and cost effective way of transferring money internationally between 2 current accounts both of which are owned by me.

They took the money instantly and I thought everything would be OK. They then sent me an email saying they needed to undertake extra checks - fair enough for an international payment. Next thing I know they have suspended my account pending a review and then without any email to me explaining the situation I find that they have terminated my account.

I appealed this decision assuming it was an automated mistake. I went through the lengthy process of providing evidence that I was who I said I was - passport photo, photo of me holding my passport, photo of me holding my passport with a Wise generated number,  3 months of my current bank statements etc. a process that took a considerable time. Within no time at all, I get an email from them saying my appeal has been rejected with absolutely no explanation as to why.

I'm therefore left totally confused. I've submitted a formal complaint but I doubt this will have any effect.

I have provided all the KYC documentation that they have asked for, I have not violated any terms of their service, I have an excellent credit rating and I've never been turned down for a financial product.

I've worked in banking for over 20 years and I fully understand the Fraud and AML regulations, however I believe Wise are hiding behind these regulations to avoid defending their arbitrary decisions to close customers' accounts. Whilst there is a clause the says they have to avoid "tipping off" fraudsters, this is in relation to actual fraud investigations. There is nothing to say they cannot provide explanations as to why they have decided to close accounts. In fact new UK regulations that came in April 2026 are compelling banks to provide reasons for account closures to avoid the process of debanking customers. Anyway, long story short - do yourself a favour and don't bother with the hassle of dealing with these clowns.

Closing at 4pm on weekends is already quite inconvenient, but what’s even more frustrating is how the staff handle the closing process.

With more than 10 minutes still left, staff start repeatedly and loudly announcing the remaining time. It happens almost every couple of minutes, and it feels less like a reminder and more like being rushed out.

Those last 10–15 minutes are usually when people are finishing their workouts, but with constant interruptions like this, it’s impossible to stay focused. It really ruins the experience.

I completely understand the need to clear the space before closing, but there are far more professional and respectful ways to do it. For example, a single reminder in the final few minutes would be more than enough.

As it stands, this approach feels quite disruptive and disrespectful to members. If this is the standard practice, it’s hard to see myself coming back.

This feels like an overpriced hotel gym, not much more.  The majority of standard equipment for a proper workout is missing ( no chest fly machine, no seated back row, no glute machine that is actually usable, etc).  The very few machines  they have are outdated and in poor condition, and they don’t get fixed fast once broken. The price per visit of nearly £ 30 and £ 80 per week ( and £180 a month) is outrageous for a basic gym with few free weights , a couple of treadmills, and few machines. Their staff is nice, though, and the place is clean . Limited weekend hours is another issue.

one_star_reviews.text:
The Deceptive Veneer
On first appearance, this establishment is a masterclass in architectural catfishing. The exterior is charming, the interior is lovely, and the initial vibe suggests a bustling, popular hotspot.

However, much like a Greek tragedy, the beauty of the set only serves to make the ensuing performance more painful. We walked in lured by glowing Google reviews, only to be met by a front-of-house energy that can only be described as "actively hostile."

​The Service (or Lack Thereof)
We were "welcomed" by an older gentleman whose disdain for his clientele was palpable. It was abundantly clear that he viewed us not as guests, but as mere obstacles between him and his paycheck. There was zero warmth, zero hospitality, and quite frankly, he didn't give a damn about our experience. To add insult to injury, any attempt at basic pleasantries or even a polite nod to the Italian language was met with the stony silence of a man who has clearly stayed in the industry three decades too long. He was, to put it bluntly, a miserable presence who sucked the joy out of the room.

​The Culinary Identity Crisis
The food was a bizarre rollercoaster of competence and catastrophe. The starters were the definition of "mid"—a solid 6/10 at best. The pâté was a particular low point; it arrived with the texture of something that had been blended into oblivion yesterday and left to contemplate its existence. It was wet, soul-less, and entirely devoid of the rustic texture one expects from a "fine" Italian kitchen. The pizza, which one assumes would be the heart of the operation, featured dough so undercooked it felt like an insult to every Italian grandmother in existence. While the toppings were fair, the foundation was soggy, uninspired, and average.

​The £40 Heartbreak
The true tragedy of the evening was my partner’s £39.99 fillet of beef. To give credit where it’s due, the chef actually knows how to handle a grill—the cooking of the steak itself was an incredible 9/10. However, the kitchen decided to sabotage its own work by drowning this beautiful cut of meat in an aggressively salty, balsamic-heavy mushroom "gravy" that obliterated any hint of quality. When you pair a ruined £40 steak with overpriced, uninspired sides and "courgette fries" that lacked any conviction, the bill becomes a very bitter pill to swallow.

​The Final Verdict
We spent over £100 for a meal that was never once validated by a "how is everything?" or a simple "thank you." We left feeling like we’d just paid for the privilege of being ignored by a staff that hates their jobs. If you read the poorest reviews on here, believe them—they are the only honest accounts of what this place has become. Lovely building, shame about the people and the execution inside it. Never again.

If I had to summarise my experience at The Fat Duck in 1 word it would be "dissapointing". We went for The Journey, celebrating their (and my) 30th birthday.

Let's start with the most important part of the experience: the dishes. They look good but the flavours are just not on a Michelin level. They're trying so hard to be different and unique but in the end it just lacks terribly in the overall taste of the dish. When we went to De Librije, a Dutch 3 star restaurant, every dish blew us away taste wise and presentation wise. "We will never be able to make this ourselves" should be the thought going through your head when tasting 3 Michelin star dishes. Take away the Fat Duck's gimmicks and most dishes were just boring tastewise, uninspiring and some downright unappetizing.

The Breakfast Cereal was just freeze dried bacon, eggs and cereal in a cold pudding(?), take away the gimmicky cereal boxes and you're left with a little bowl of bacon and egg porridge, not even worthy of 1 Michelin Star. The "walk in the woods" course tasted like something left in a wet barn for the last 40 years.

The atmosphere of the restaurant itself is another dissapointment. The design is sober and outdated, like you're back in 2005 when the restaurant was at it's peak. Everything is cramped, you have no privacy because the tables are as close together as in a pizzaria. There are always 7-8 staff members running around on the floor which makes it feel chaotic and not relaxed. The staff themselves were a mix of funny quick witted veterans (Nothing bad to say there) and AI robots who just recited their verses and left the table.

We had the Discovery wine pairing with the dishes, but between every dish before we could finish our previous glasses they were already pouring in new glasses, making it feel very rushed and unappreciated. We were dining at their tempo, not the other way around like it should be at this level.

Honestly It was a waste of our money and time (we came from The Netherlands to the UK only for this experience), and next time we won't believe the fake hype and do our research before booking something as expensive and supossedly special as this.

This was not a casual request — it was based on official government guidance and safety concerns.

What’s worse is this clearly isn’t an isolated issue — there are multiple reviews from other customers facing the exact same problem, particularly for Dubai bookings.

To make matters worse, family members travelling on the exact same dates with another provider (Love Holidays) received full refunds without even asking for it. The contrast in how customers are treated is shocking.

I am also travelling with a five-month-old baby, yet they still expect customers to proceed despite FCDO advice. That alone says everything about their priorities.

I’ve now had to escalate this through American Express, who have already recognised the validity of my claim and taken action.

Overall, this feels like customers are being forced into a corner and left to fight for money they are legally entitled to. I would strongly advise others to avoid booking with this company, especially when things don’t go to plan.
if you want disappointment be sure to book with these guys. The worst on the market.

Absolutely terrible experience on our honeymoon.

While we were in Zanzibar, our return flight was cancelled due to the situation in the Middle East — something we understand was out of anyone’s control. However, the way Best At Travel handled the situation was completely unacceptable.

We were initially told to wait 72 hours before our flight for our agent to contact us. Despite the flight being officially cancelled, we heard nothing. When we chased this, we were reassured it was their duty of care to get us home but to ‘wait our turn’.

Two days before we were due to fly, we were offered an extremely complicated route (Tanzania → Kenya → Uganda → London Gatwick → London Heathrow → Edinburgh). Upon researching, we discovered we would need a yellow fever vaccination even for transit — something we did not have. When we raised this concern, our agent dismissed it and told us it “wouldn’t matter,” which felt both reckless and irresponsible.

Feeling we had no other option, we agreed to proceed, but the flights were never ticketed. Communication throughout was poor and inconsistent — we were passed between staff, told conflicting information, and at one point informed our agent was no longer dealing with us without any handover.

Customer service was also extremely disappointing, with one representative being particularly rude and dismissive. At one stage, we were even asked why we kept calling as they had “other customers around the world,” which made us feel completely unimportant.

The situation escalated further when we were told Qatar Airways would not approve the route and that we should instead wait to be repatriated — Best At Travel’s only offer was 3 nights of accommodation covered, and any additional stay at our own expense. This was incredibly stressful, especially as there was and still is no clear timeline for repatriation. (3.5 weeks later).

Out of desperation, we agreed to pay for alternative flights ourselves, costing several thousand pounds — only for these to fail due to visa/ETA issues that should have been identified beforehand. We then had to attempt booking flights ourselves at the last minute, incurring even more costs and having to miss a week of work as the first flights we could get home was 5 days later.

To make matters worse, when we arrived at the hotel that was supposedly booked for us, there was no reservation in place and we were refused entry. We were left stranded with no access to customer service, as their lines had been switched off. After repeated attempts, we finally got through to someone via their sales line. When our agent eventually called back, he was abrupt and unprofessional, even shouting at hotel reception staff.

This experience completely ruined the final week of our honeymoon, causing significant stress, anxiety, and uncertainty at a time that should have been special.

Since returning, communication has been equally poor. We have not received refunds owed for cancelled flights, and responses have been next to nothing. Escalating the issue to the CEO was also useless. She advised nothing was going to be done to resolve the issue and then passed us over to guest relations who told us to wait 28 days… probably for them to tell us again they aren’t going to do anything even though we’ve asked for a refund or compensation for the days they ruined due to not communicating or booking us new flights in a timely manner.

Overall, the handling of this situation was extremely disappointing. A travel agent should provide support and guidance when things go wrong — not add to the stress with poor communication, lack of accountability, and unsafe travel suggestions.

I would not recommend Best At Travel to anyone… i’d suggest using Trail Finders instead.  After speaking to several people in Zanzibar whose flight got cancelled, Trail Finders booked new flights quickly and efficiently!

Thieves! Used twice, NEVER again!

I had a Dubai trip for Easter scheduled for April 2nd – 12th 2026. £6440 was paid in full and then the Middle East war started. I was conscious that Best at Travel (BaT) would be dealing with customers either already in the Middle East or due to travel imminently, so I didn’t contact them right away. On March 18th Emirates Airlines gave the green light for those travelling within my dates to cancel their trips so I contacted the agent I had liaised with at BaT to process my cancellation and refund. I was disgusted to be told that BaT would not begin the process my refund ‘in house’ until it was 1 week from the date of departure and it would then take a further 6-8 weeks for me to receive the £6440 refund, In fact the exact words he used were “we can’t refund everyone at once of we’ll go bust”. I reminded him of The Package Travel and Linked Travel Arrangements Regulations 2018 mandate that states that travellers should receive a full refund within 14 days if a package holiday is cancelled by the organiser… I was ignored.

Right now, I am £6440 out of pocket with nothing to show for it, unable to book another holiday with my family until they refund me, and I’m being told that is likely to be at the end of May 2026, meaning I’ll miss the opportunity to take my children on holiday for the May half term too. These crooks are unlawful and unhelpful… avoid at all costs!

Very disappointing and unprofessional experience.

I made every effort to attend my appointment on time and left home early. However, due to industrial strike disruptions on the Underground (Central and Hammersmith lines), I was delayed beyond my control. I contacted the clinic in advance and left a voicemail explaining the situation.

One of the key issues is the location itself. The clinic is not easily accessible by public transport, especially during disruptions, which is something they should be mindful of. In addition, it is located on the first floor, which is highly inconvenient for patients with mobility or spinal issues.

After finally arriving — already physically exhausted and in visible discomfort — I was met with a very cold and unwelcoming reception. There was no attempt to understand the situation or show any basic empathy.

This was particularly concerning given that I had already completed their medical form in detail, clearly outlining my lower back condition, mobility limitations, anxiety, ADHD, and other relevant issues. I was also wearing a visible anxiety awareness lanyard, which made my condition even more apparent.

Despite all of this, the only focus was on the fact that I was late, with no consideration of the circumstances or my health condition.

Overall, this experience lacked professionalism, empathy, and basic patient care awareness. I would not recommend this clinic, especially for individuals with existing physical or mental health conditions.

Response to Owner:

Thank you for your reply.

After reading not only your response to me, but also your responses to several other negative reviews, it becomes even clearer that the issue is not simply one delayed appointment, but a repeated pattern of defensive responses, lack of accountability, and very little genuine patient care.

I fully understand appointment schedules and I never expected special treatment. I left home early, informed the clinic in advance, and the Underground strike on the Central and Hammersmith lines was completely outside my control — something you yourself acknowledged.

However, the real issue was never just lateness.

It was the cold and dismissive reception from the moment I arrived, despite attending with genuine medical conditions involving spinal pain, lower back issues, mobility limitations, anxiety, and ADHD — all clearly declared in your own medical forms.

For a clinic treating patients with pain and mobility difficulties, being located on the first floor and far from accessible transport should create more understanding, not less.

I attended already aware of your treatment plans, packages, and offers, with the intention of becoming a long-term patient if the experience felt professional and trustworthy. Unfortunately, the first impression made that impossible.

Professional healthcare is not only about schedules — it is about empathy, respect, and how patients are treated when they arrive already in pain.

This review reflects exactly that.

Considering both the distance and the overall experience, it is simply more reasonable for me to continue treatment with larger and more established providers such as # Chiropractic First, where professionalism and patient care are clearly a priority.

I had a very disappointing experience at Peugeot Thames Slough.

I visited the dealership to ask for some basic help and information regarding a car I had already purchased from another Peugeot dealership. When I first arrived, I asked if anyone was available to assist me and was told everyone was busy. I said that was completely fine. The receptionist, who was polite and helpful, suggested I wait in case someone became available.

However, it wasn’t clear where the waiting area was, so I stayed near the reception. During this time, multiple staff members walked past me repeatedly without acknowledging me or offering any assistance.

Eventually, a staff member approached me and, rather than offering help, spoke to me in a rude and dismissive manner, asking “what do you want?” I explained my situation, but he immediately told me to go back to the dealership where I bought the car. He stated that they wouldn’t help me because I had given my money to another dealership, claiming they were a different franchise and even said “we are not Peugeot,” despite the clear branding and confirmation from reception that they are.

He then told me to “drive or walk 50 miles” back to the original dealership, which was completely unnecessary and unprofessional, especially as I was only asking for basic information about a car from the brand they represent.

The situation escalated further when he threatened to have me escorted out, simply because I wasn’t standing in a clearly marked waiting area that no one had shown me. When I asked what would happen if I wanted to buy another car from them, he dismissively replied that I didn’t and told me to go away.

This level of customer service is completely unacceptable. I understand that staff may be busy, but there is no excuse for being rude, dismissive, and confrontational. The receptionist was the only positive part of the experience—she was courteous and professional.

Unfortunately, this interaction has completely put me off ever considering buying a car from this dealership in the future.

I do not usually post things like this, but after the last few weeks I have had trying to sort out issues with Thames Motor Group in Slough, I feel I have to.
In December 2024, I paid £32,000 for a brand new Jeep Renegade from Thames Motor Group. It had 11 miles on the clock.
On 19 February 2026, the car completely broke down. The RAC attended after 6 hours and confirmed it was a major issue and not fixable. The car was taken straight back to the dealership.
Within 24 hours, I was told the engine had completely failed and needed replacing.
After doing my own checks, I discovered the car was subject to a recall at the time it was sold to me. I was never told this.
Let that sink in. I paid £32,000 for a brand new car that had an unresolved recall issue affecting the engine.
I had also raised concerns early on about warning lights on the dashboard, but these were dismissed with excuses.
For context, I was only driving the car around 20 miles a week, so it took time for the issue to fully show itself.
The experience that followed was just as concerning as the fault itself.
• The car was sold to me with an active recall issue
• This was never disclosed at the point of sale
• No one contacted me at any stage to inform me of the recall
• No one asked me to bring the car back to fix it
• I was unknowingly driving a potentially unsafe vehicle
• When it broke down, the seriousness was initially downplayed
• I was told I would receive a call from senior management, which never happened
• Calls and emails were not returned
• The overall customer service was poor and dismissive
I was then told that because the car is under warranty, they would simply replace the engine and return the car to me.
That completely misses the point.
This should never have happened on a brand new car. Selling a vehicle with an unresolved recall, without disclosure, is not acceptable.
I have been buying cars for over 40 years and I have never experienced anything like this.
When you spend £32,000, you expect a level of professionalism and responsibility. This fell well below that standard.
My advice to anyone considering buying from Thames Motor Group is simple:
Do your own checks. Use the GOV.UK recall checker. Do not assume everything has been done properly, even when buying from a main dealer.
This has been a very frustrating experience and I will not be using Thames Motor Group again. I am now taking legal advice on the matter.

I specifically asked if anything further was needed from me, including payment beforehand, and was assured everything had been added correctly and payment could be dealt with upon completion.

I then dropped the car off.

The following day — over 24 hours later — I called for an update and was astonishingly told that they could not even locate my vehicle. Eventually they “found” it, only to admit it had not even been looked at yet. On top of that, nobody seemed to know anything about the sidesteps I had arranged weeks earlier.

The next evening, around 5pm, I received a call advising that diagnostics had finally been carried out and they now knew what the issue was — but it still wouldn’t be repaired for several more days. I explained I needed the vehicle that weekend and was then told: “Well, the car only arrived yesterday.”

Except it hadn’t.

The car had already been sitting there for well over a day at that point.

Then came another revelation: the sidesteps hadn’t been ordered or arranged correctly either. Somehow, their system stated there was “an issue with the sidesteps” rather than recording that I wanted them installed while the vehicle was there. Completely different thing.

I collected the car and returned it the following week after being rebooked in.

Upon arrival for the second booking, they once again could not find my booking.

After eventually locating it, the technician repeated the exact same misunderstanding regarding the sidesteps — again insisting they believed the sidesteps themselves were faulty. I had to explain for yet another time that I wanted sidesteps FITTED, not repaired.

At this stage I escalated matters to Brian, the Customer Service Manager, who assured me everything had now been corrected on the system and that the vehicle would take approximately 3–4 days to repair.

That was on a Tuesday.

I then called on Thursday for an update and was told someone would call me back. Nobody did.

On Friday, I finally received a call informing me they were waiting for a part that would not arrive until JULY. At that same moment, I was also told the sidestep issue still hadn’t been properly updated on the system.

Let that sink in.

This vehicle had now been in multiple times, sat there for days at a time, and only after all of that was I eventually told they didn’t even have the required part and wouldn’t have it for around TWO MONTHS.

So why exactly was the car kept there for several more days if the issue had already supposedly been diagnosed?

Nobody could answer that.

In fact, that became the theme of the entire experience.

Every time I called the service department, the line either cut out, rang endlessly, or I simply could not get through. Every time I finally managed to speak to someone, the answer was always the same:

“I don’t know.”

That phrase was repeated so often it became almost comical.

Even Brian, the Customer Service Manager, eventually shrugged his shoulders and repeated the exact same words when asked why everything had gone so catastrophically wrong:

“I don’t know.”

For a brand positioned as the pinnacle of luxury motoring, the aftersales experience was shockingly disorganised, poorly communicated, and utterly lacking accountability.

Premium vehicles come with premium price tags because customers expect premium service.

Unfortunately, this experience delivered the exact opposite.

I recently brought my car in for its 4 year service at this dealer, and the experience was incredibly frustrating from start to finish.

The workmanship was remarkably sloppy. The service indicators were never reset, and the technicians failed to reinstall the plastic retaining clips. This left loose panels and fasteners hanging freely in the engine compartment.

Attempting to resolve this has been impossible:
1) Unhelpful Phone Support: When I called, they simply told me to bring the car back in myself, offering no real accommodation for their own poor workmanship.

2) Blocked Communication: My complaint emails to the service colleage and main Lookers email keep bouncing back as spam. I filled out the online contact form but received zero response. I even made a separate new car enquiry and cannot reply to the sales team's emails due to the exact same spam-filter issue.

3) Poor Service Experience: Courtesy car appointments are completely unavailable for months and the dealership is in the middle of nowhere so no transport back unless you drive another car or take a taxi back to Aylesbury.

I was locked into this dealer network via a service plan, otherwise I would not have booked the car with them. I've had far better experience with the dealer for my main car and dealers in Oxford. 1 out of 5 star unfortunately.

I approached Duncan Lewis urgently for help with a family law matter involving a non-molestation order hearing.

Unfortunately, my experience was extremely poor. I received no meaningful response before the hearing, no indication that they were considering whether they could help, and no practical guidance while the matter was still live and urgent. Their eventual reply came around two weeks after the hearing had already taken place, simply stating that they did not have capacity to take the case on.

Thankfully, the hearing was relatively straightforward and, as a litigant in person, I was able to deal with it myself and the application against me was dismissed. However, that does not change how poor the service felt from the point of view of someone seeking urgent legal help.

Had the matter been more complex, or had I been more vulnerable, the lack of communication could have left me in a very difficult position. In my view, if a firm cannot assist with an urgent matter, they should say so promptly rather than leaving someone with no clarity.

Their response suggested that I seek alternative representation via the Law Society website. Based on my experience, I think that is very good advice, and I would pass that recommendation on to others considering Duncan Lewis for urgent family law assistance.

I could not recommend Duncan Lewis based on my experience. Others in a similar position may be better served by finding a firm that responds more professionally and in a timely manner.

**Update following Duncan Lewis’ response:**

Duncan Lewis have now replied to this review asking me to contact their Client Care Team so they can “look into this matter further” and “address any concerns”.

In my view, everything they need to know is already set out clearly in the review above. I contacted them urgently for help with a live family law matter. I did not receive a meaningful response before the hearing. Their reply came around two weeks after the hearing had already taken place, by which point I had represented myself and the application against me had been dismissed.

I struggle to see what can usefully be addressed now, especially if they are unable to identify the issue from the review itself. To me, that does rather reinforce my concern that attention to detail may be lacking.

When someone is seeking urgent legal assistance, clear communication and timely responses matter. Based on my experience, I would question whether the handling of my enquiry reflects the level of care and attention someone should expect when dealing with a legal matter.

My original review stands.
It is also interesting that it took approximately four weeks to respond to an urgent request for legal assistance, but only around four hours to respond to a critical Google review.

People can draw their own conclusions from that.

one_star_reviews.text:
I'm unhappy with the professional standards and conduct of Fusion Consulting group.In or around June 2025, my company engaged Fusion Consultancy for tax planning and advisory services at a cost of approx £21,000. The service was presented to me as a comprehensive and bespoke tax strategy for both company and personal matters.

The service sold to me was materially misrepresented and fell significantly below the professional standards I would expect from an ATT-affiliated practice.

Fusion have used misleading representations regarding scope of services.
The proposal documentation referred to the “Delivery of Master Tax Strategy”, which reasonably implies a complete planning and delivery service. At no stage was it made sufficiently clear that the £21,000 fee related primarily to a written report only, and that substantial additional implementation fees would later be demanded.

In fact, after receiving the report, I was informed that implementation of the recommendations would require a further payment of approximately £21,000. Bringing the total cost to £42,000

Had this been made transparently clear from the outset, I would never have agreed to proceed as this would not be financially justified for our business.

In actual fact. I had originally declined Fusions services, stating that I thought the cost was not proportionate to the saving I would make. This then lead to Mitch Young (director of Fusion) making misleading assurances regarding value and financial benefit
He said:
“I can certainly assure you that the savings you would make short and long term would significantly outweigh the costs.” (e mail dated 12th June 8.37am)

At no point within these discussions was it properly clarified that substantial additional implementation fees would be required before any alleged savings could realistically be achieved. Mitch Young painted a picture that with £21k we would see savings that far outweighed this cost. He never mentioned that an additional £21k would be needed, bringing the total to £42k. I believe this created a misleading impression that the quoted fee covered the overall planning and delivery process.

Mitch went one step further to get us past the line. He made assurances that if my company did not make savings that outweighed the cost, he would refund us. This was what offered me the assurance I needed.

Fusion produced a report for us for tax planning. I was shocked when they requested another £21k to implement ANY of the steps in the report. I had up until this point been under the impression we were paying for an end to end service. My company cannot pay £42k for tax implementation. this means the £21k we paid was literally for only a report, that will not deliver any level of saving unless I pay further to implement anything.

The report itself is of my opinion, a non-bespoke product. This is because the report contained another individual’s name and company details within the document. This strongly indicated that the report had been adapted from pre-existing material rather than prepared specifically for my circumstances.

I experienced what I considered inappropriate professional conduct from the Director, who attempted to contact me via personal TikTok direct messages despite me being a paying client. When the point was raised, he swiftly deleted this account and his complaints handler has outright denied any communication of a personal nature via Tik Tok.

When I had requested a partial refund for the above breaches in professional standards and conduct. Fusion have refused, going as far as threatening me for leaving a review of my experience. They have also made a statement saying that consumer rights don't apply as it was my company that engaged in their service. What they fail to understand is that as a member of the ATT they are obligated and bound by certain rules, one of which is that they must not engage in misleading or deceptive conduct.

Very poor experience dealing with Copart.

I purchased a vehicle that was clearly misrepresented in the auction listing. The description stated the boot was stuck closed, but the vehicle arrived with the boot already open, revealing structural damage. They likely said the boot was stuck closed to avoid taking photos inside the boot.

On top of that, there was additional damage to the vehicle that was not present in the listing photographs. I can only assume this damage occurred after the photos were taken, either in the salvage yard or during the auction process. This concern was dismissed by relying on a disclaimer that vehicles may have more damage than shown, despite this appearing to be new damage caused after the vehicle had already been listed.

The vehicle also has four punctured tyres, hard to proved but again no present in the auction photos, in the photos the tyres were inflated.

In my view, they are not transparent about the true condition of vehicles and, in this case, it appeared there was a clear attempt to conceal damage and mislead buyers.

The vehicle was later reclassified from Cat N to Cat S, confirming the original listing was inaccurate. Initially, I was offered just £300 compensation for this change in category, which is nowhere near the loss in value when a vehicle moves from Cat N to Cat S.

What should have been a straightforward resolution became a long and frustrating complaints process, with repeated delays, changing positions, and poor communication. I only received a refund after repeatedly challenging their response and making it clear that I was prepared to take court action.

Would not use again. Avoid buying from them.

I asked whether a replacement car could be sent, but was told the wait would be at least another hour. I then received a further call from the company apologising and again confirming that I would be refunded.

Despite this, I was still charged for the journey (£177.07). Seven days later, I still have not received my refund. I have sent numerous emails, only to be told they have tracking information showing the car arrived early and that the journey was completed — which is completely untrue.

I have also called multiple times and each time I am told the message has been passed on, yet nobody resolves the issue or follows up properly.

AVOID THIS COMPANY. I am still chasing my refund.

I made a booking through minicabit, paid online, and received confirmation. However, after 24 hours, the booking was cancelled without any explanation or prior notification—no email, no message, nothing.

When I contacted their live chat, I was told the booking had failed a “fraud test.” This was confusing and concerning, as the payment had already been processed successfully and no further clarification was provided.

Overall, the experience felt unreliable and poorly handled. It appears that if an operator is unable to fulfil a job, the customer is left without support or a clear resolution. There seems to be a lack of accountability and customer care, which raises concerns about the level of security and service provided.

I've had a bad experience this morning - cab did not arrive to take my mother to the airport at 8 this am; it took 30 minutes to contact a person who claimed the passenger had already been picked up (she had not).  They were not able to action a refund on the phone; I also emailed support email but have not heard back and concerned that ball is now in my court to get my money back for a service that was not provided.

End result: I got a refund about 36 hours later after minicabits 'investigation' to confirm my mom had not been picked up - overall I would have much preferred to book a cab with someone who can tell me what is going on with my cab in real time.  So will be booking direct with minicab companies in future.

Mismanaged and dishonest!! We ordered a transfer service from central London to Gatwick airport clearly stating 2 passengers and 4 suitcases and were pre-charged for the journey. The car sent us was a mini Toyota Prius!! The driver was extremely unhelpful and did not even attempt to fit the luggage, lectured us about some regulations and drove off leaving us stressed about missing our flight! When we filed a complaint we were told that our HAND LUGGAGE which was one tiny carry on was not stated in our booking, as if the Prius had space for 4 suitcases and the driver put in even a dime of effort, and it was our fault and therefore we were not entitled m for any compensation. If you value your time, money and peace of mind DO NOT book from this horrible service.

I'm surprised they're still operating.

10 years ago one driver from the airport taxis firm they subcontracted the trip to arrived 15mins late, didn't know his way, stuck in 15mins in a roadworks, then spent 40mins driving at half speed through residential area instead heading on expressway to airport. almost missed flight and had to run to get to gate.

On the way home the booked driver arrived late then dragged me to car at high speed ignoring my own pace, then was using a phone stuck to his steering wheel to book journeys, look at flight arrival logs etc the entire time, ignoring the road and driving dangerously.

The company couldn't even understand my complaints afterwards and tried to offer me £15 off my next trip as if I'd ever book with such an incompetent firm again.

Reported the one driver to public carriage office for dangerous driving.

No accountability and trips are outsourced to random other operators so they cannot keep any oversight of who is taking on the trips and journeys. I'm sure the customer service is also outsourced.

Use registered black taxis for airport journeys.

The extra £15-20 price is still life saving compared to nearly being driven off the road by incompetent drivers.

Using SEO to get to top of search on google =/= competence or safe service.

Even Uber would be more accountable at this point.

My experience with this company was an absolute disaster and extremely stressful.

It all started fairly normally: I called to arrange a car recovery service, and they politely assured me that a vehicle would arrive shortly. To be fair, they did arrive on time, loaded my car, and took it away “for repairs,” promising everything would be done within 3–4 days.

That’s where the nightmare began.

Once the car was in their possession, communication completely changed. After 4–5 days, I was simply told that the car was “ready” and that I had to pay £1,850. At no point was the cost discussed in advance. No one called to explain what repairs were needed or to ask for my approval. You are simply presented with a bill and expected to pay.

What’s worse, they refuse to disclose where the vehicle is being kept or which garage is carrying out the work. Instead, they send you bank details and demand payment — only after that will they tell you where your car is. This lack of transparency is extremely concerning.

Collecting the vehicle turned into another ordeal. The agreed times were constantly changed, and no one stuck to any arrangement. When I finally arrived at the agreed location, the driver was over 1.5 hours late, repeatedly delaying their arrival.

As for the quality of the repair — I have serious doubts. I never received a proper invoice detailing the work carried out or the parts used. My requests for documentation were simply ignored. Eventually, I was sent a handwritten invoice with no company details whatsoever, which is completely unprofessional and unacceptable.

In summary: zero transparency, poor communication, unauthorised charges, constant delays, and highly questionable service quality.

I strongly advise against using this company. You risk paying a significant amount of money while receiving poor service — and potentially ending up in a situation where your car is effectively being held somewhere unknown.

I used Carter Electrical for an EICR and the experience was a lesson in predatory billing. I paid £300 for the initial inspection, which identified a 'loose connection' (a C2 fault).

I was then given a remedial estimate of £264, justified as a 'worst-case scenario' that included investigating the circuit and replacing parts (an MCB). However, the actual repair took only 20 minutes, required zero parts, and was simply a loose earth wire in a socket—exactly what the first report had already suspected.

When I challenged the £264 estimate, they pulled a very cheeky move: They re-issued the invoice for £222, stripping out the mention of 'worst-case' repairs and parts from the description, yet kept the labor charge nearly identical. They essentially admitted the work was a minor, best-case scenario fix but refused to lower the price to reflect a standard 20-minute call-out.

As a landlord, I felt I had no choice but to pay just to get the Satisfactory certificate I needed for legal compliance. If you want a firm that bills fairly for the work actually performed—rather than just whatever they can get away with—I would suggest looking elsewhere.

Update 07/04/26:
Following the owner’s public response above promising a "refund or credit," I reached out to the office as requested. Privately, their tone changed completely. They flatly refused any refund or adjustment, claiming that returning £90 of the £222 bill (for a 20-minute fix) would cause the business a "financial loss."

It is clear the public apology was a PR tactic to save face on Google, with no actual intention of resolving the billing discrepancy. I have paid over £520 in total to this company for a 2-hour inspection and a 20-minute repair. Future customers should be aware that the "professional" and "transparent" persona shown here in the comments does not match the private reality. Buyer beware.

To the lady in the red coat; I seldom write bad reviews towards the hospitality industry as I live and breath it daily at a high level. Mishaps, misunderstandings and inconveniences are a part of service. In this instance, though, I believe the service at this bar on Sunday night was so poor that it needs to be addressed.

Greeted with open arms at 11:30pm, we were advised the venue was closing at midnight. Being a group of 4, all of whom work in hospitality in managerial positions, we understand clearly that it is necessary on the staffs behalf to advise us and doable on ours to be in-and-out in that time.

We sat, ordered within minutes, and we're in for a bottle of red and two cocktails amounting to a sum just shy of £250. Upon ordering we were advised: "We are closing in 25 minutes." No hassle.

We were then prompted once again, barely 5 minutes later, by a different server, that the venue was closing soon. And then moments later, by a different person, we were told in a relatively rude fashion: "You have to pay the bill now." To which we responded, "That's fine, can we have the bill." Upon paying we were, once again, almost comically at this point, reminded of the closing time in 15 minutes. The bottle was half full, our cocktails were finished, the bill was paid. There was no indication of any pressing issue.

But to end it all in what quite literally and metaphorically appeared to be the cherry on top of this experience, a fourth and final woman dressed in a long red coat whom we'd had no encounter with yet, walked up to the table and without saying so much as an excuse me, pokes her head over the table and says "We are closing in 10 minutes." Before walking away and spending the next few minutes itching around our table and ready to step foot outside to go home not a second past midnight, clear from the bright red raincoat she wore as she paced around glaring.

It was laughable... and we did, in fact, laugh for the rest of the night after we left (on-time) at the obvious lack of communication between the staff, and the direction of the management to treat us as hostile in such an establishement after we had paid good money and showed no signs of being a problem table. It is such poor form to witness this, and as seasoned hospitality folk ourselves, this was simply an embarrassing demonstration on behalf of the closing staff.

It is important to remember what we do, and who we do it for, regardless of wether we know it or not. The bright lights, expensive sofas and extensive cocktail selection is only as admirable as those who present them. We will not be coming back, but we will use you as an example of what not to do.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am writing this review as a concerned parent following a serious safeguarding concern involving an unexplained injury to my 14-month-old son.
When I collected my child, I noticed a visible bruise on his forehead. This had not been communicated to me by any member of staff during the day or at the time of pickup. When I raised the concern, I received inconsistent responses — one staff member stated that my child had been outside, while another said he had not. Notably, his shoes were new and showed no signs of outdoor use. More concerningly, I was told that staff had not even noticed the bruise.
The following day, the bruise became significantly more visible and reddish. From the photos taken before, it appeared that my child may have bumped his forehead again in the same place. Despite this, there was still no communication, no incident report, and no acknowledgment from staff.
As a parent, I understand that minor accidents can happen, especially with toddlers. However, the lack of awareness, inconsistent information, absence of incident reporting, and failure to inform me promptly was deeply concerning. Transparency and communication are essential when entrusting a nursery with the care of a young child.
Due to these ongoing concerns, I made the decision to withdraw my son from the nursery with immediate effect. Only after I requested his withdrawal did the nursery initiate an investigation. I was advised that this would be followed up; however, 28 days passed and I did not receive any update or outcome.
This experience raised serious concerns about supervision, safeguarding procedures, and communication within the nursery.

The Cappadocia hotel was located on the edge of Avanos, in a field with just two other hotels, some 2.5 miles to the centre of Avanos. For example to see the waterfall falling into the sea in Antalya 45 minutes was allocated. Not only that but it meant always arriving around 6pm or later to our hotel. The way RSD promotes the tour is that there are optional excursions. It's only after you pay for the tour that you get informed that you can't pick or choose these excursions as they are only offered as a package, all or nothing. Long review but necessary. I had a LHD Spanish car to sell urgently (you only get 14 days from arriving in the UK before you need to do import dutie, new mot, new plates etc) and with just a few days to go I finally got a response from one out lots of LHD car buyer dealers that I had messaged. So, I had answered all enquiries from Ray honestly and openly.
I emailed him 5 pictures (that was as much as the email would attach) and he offered me a price. Naturally with a small variable depending on evaluation in person.
I got up at 5:30 am to do the drive of 4.5 hours to meet up and do the sale and a guy called Alex turned up.
Lots of huffing and puffing ensued about the condition of the car. (It's 18 years old but mechanically very sound, high spec, not beaten up/dented and lots of work recently done in Spain before I drove back to England)
But apparently, the leather interior was in 'terrible' condition and I hadn't shown Ray photos of that (its aged leather with cracks but not open rips or deep or peeling off) But when I said that Ray hadn't even asked me for any extra photos before offering a rough estimate, he put me on the phone to Ray who just shouted over me on the phone as if I was the problem and he'd been somehow inconvenienced rather than me - though I'm the one who had driven hours to get there.  I'd have taken any extra pictures or videos he wanted  but he never asked for more than the ones I had sent him.
I had also told him there was partial service history and I had put it through a service, had timing belt done and new ITV (Spanish mot) last month before driving back to the UK.
(I spent €2,200 on it in the few short weeks I had it)
But although he hadn't asked for exactly what service history there was, until I was stood there with Alex. He made out like I was trying to deceive him because unfortunately (due to the sad circumstances of my leaving Spain rapidly) I didn't realise the proof of service and timing belt wasn't among the papers in the car. There was some receipts but not all them.
Now, I understand the value of receipts for jobs but the way he spoke to me was awful.
I ended up cryng from the stress and way I was treated.
I had to call the garage in Spain whilst crying, to ask them to look on their system to find my history with them and prove what had been done.
I wasn't able to do this on my phone because typically it was that very day whilst travelling that my phone number got ported from one provider to another, so I was without satnav and messaging capability (adding to the stress of the whole day) But again, Ray made out like I was using that as an excuse and was just lying and I should have automatically known to just call Spain on Alex's phone!!
Funny enough, Alex had plugged in one of those ECU readers to check for any problems and only the issues that came up were electrical - mainly related to the central locking which I had openly told Ray about.

Really? I've driven down the country from Northumberland and he knew I only had 2 days left to sell before having to do the import nightmare.
So they had me over a barrel between a rock and a hard place.
I had no option but to take a massive loss. But of course made to seem like they're doing me a favour.
So if you see an expensive Ssangyong Rexton on their site shortly - just know they treated an already vulnerable woman appallingly to get it for next to nothing.

If I could give 0 stars, I would. The car itself seemed fine at the beginning, but then, within 6 months, we had 3 different and COSTLY problems with the car. Within those 6 months, we were covered by the warranty, meaning Grant had to legally pay for the issues as they were issues that came with the car upon purchase and for those issues under the Consumer Rights Act 2015. He sold us a faulty car and claimed that it had been checked over before the sale.

We went to different and independent mechanics, and they all said that the car had barely received an inspection before sale, it was just enough to pass the MOT. When contacting Grant, not only did he tells us we had to pay to fix those things out of our own pockets as he has a small business and cannot afford to pay for these things (even though the warranty and the law says he must do so), he is currently trying to force us to pay him back for 1/3 of the problems he helped to pay for. And the cherry on top: he is threatening to take US TO COURT for something that could have been avoided if he had carried out an adequate inspection of the car.

We were met with: A flat battery which had to get completely replaced, 4 worn out break pads which were a safety issue and had to get replaced, and just last week, we had a loose piece at the front of the car; the crank pulley was loose, very worn out, and making noises when driving. The total of all of this was a whooping cost of £900, £400 of which we paid, £500 of which he is asking us to pay half of, as if he wasn't legally required to pay the £500 anyway.

Grant doesn't operate on a good faith basis, he wants to sell you a car full of problems and blame it on you when you try to take it up with him. He is nice and kind at the beginning to make you feel bad for trying to make him pay for the car, with the excuse that he is a "small business", even though he is legally required to pay. I really hate leaving negative reviews, and avoid them when I can, but when it comes to something as serious and as expensive as a car, this is no longer a joking matter. And I see I am not alone in this given I have seen plently of reviews pointing to the same issue.

Avoid this dealership if you can, and hold Grant to account where he is trying to avoid liability for the faulty products he is selling.

Worse ultrasound appointment with unprofessional sonographer

This has been one of the most unprofessional and frustrating healthcare experiences I have ever had.

My first ultrasound appointment was on 16 March 2026. I arrived only 5 minutes late and was refused entry and told to rebook. I accepted this and was given a second appointment on 10 April 2026.

For that appointment, I arrived 30 minutes early, followed all instructions, drank 2 litres of water, and held my bladder for the scan. Despite this, I was told the scan could not be done because the sonographer’s colleague was not available. Then I was told my appointment had to be cancelled because the staff member had a GP appointment. I was clearly told there was no way my scan could be done.

I was reassured that I did not need to do anything and that a new appointment would be arranged. After waiting a week with no update, I called and was shocked to be told that I had “not attended” my appointment. No rebooking had been made, and false information was added to my record.

As a midwife myself, I find this completely unacceptable. Cancelling a patient, failing to rebook, and then marking them as non-attendance is a serious breach of professional standards.

I have now been given another appointment on 15 June 2026 — almost 5 months since December — despite needing this scan following abnormal blood test results. This delay is not only negligent but could potentially impact patient care.

The lack of accountability, poor communication, and disregard for patient wellbeing is extremely concerning. I also feel deeply uncomfortable with how I was treated and cannot ignore the possibility of discriminatory behaviour.

This situation needs urgent investigation. I will be escalating this matter to higher authorities.

When the car was eventually returned, it had sustained damage to the front bumper, wheel arch and headlamp units which was not present when the vehicle was collected. I also discovered that approximately 800 miles had been added to the odometer while the car was in the mechanic’s possession, without my permission. The police later tracked the number plate and informed me that the car had been spotted driving in many locations far away from where the mechanic was based.

To make matters worse, the invoice for the work referenced a limited company that had already been dissolved many months before the booking. Despite repeated requests, I was never provided with clear insurance details.

I ultimately had to:
* pursue a chargeback through Amex
* report the matter to Hertfordshire Constabulary
* issue a Letter Before Action
* begin Small Claims Court proceedings to recover the cost of repairing the damage, which I wasn’t able to do

ClickMechanic did remove the mechanic from the platform after I raised concerns, but ultimately took the position that they are only an introductory marketplace and accepted no liability for what happened.

I appreciate that marketplaces cannot control every individual mechanic, but I relied heavily on the company’s marketing around vetting, trust and customer protection when deciding to hand over my vehicle.

I’m left with a damaged car and a court process which has yielded no results. Even the police have been unable to track down this ‘vetted’ mechanic. He has disappeared off the surface of the earth - and didn’t live at the address supplied to ClickMechanic.

Based on my experience, I would strongly advise others against using this platform. Do not give over your car to a mechanic through this platform, as ClickMechanic will accept absolutely no responsibility if something goes wrong.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’m extremely disappointed with my experience. I underwent rhinoplasty to correct a noticeably crooked nose and a visible lump. While the surgeon did slightly reduce the lump from the profile view, the overall result is far from what was promised. One side of my nose was essentially left untouched, and it remains visibly uneven and crooked. I questioned whether he forgot about that side and even he seemed visibly surprised at the state of it.

The changes made were minimal to the point of being barely noticeable, especially considering the significant cost of the procedure. I expected a meaningful improvement, but instead I feel like very little was actually done.

What is even more frustrating is the lack of accountability during the follow-up. I was told that this was “the best that could be done,” which felt dismissive and did not reflect the concerns I raised. There was no willingness to acknowledge the unsatisfactory outcome vs what he had deemed a completely reasonable and achievable goal pre-op and he did not discuss potential solutions, not that I would trust him with any more money for a second operation.

I completely understand that, in many cases, achieving the desired outcome from rhinoplasty may require more than one procedure. However, I feel misled by the clear gap between what was promised and the actual result. If this outcome was a likely limitation, I would have expected that to be communicated transparently from the outset. An experienced surgeon should set realistic expectations and clearly explain what can and cannot be achieved, rather than agreeing to results that ultimately were not delivered.

Overall, this was a costly experience with disappointing results. I regret going ahead with this surgeon and would not recommend them based on my experience.

I’ve had a pretty frustrating experience with Cuckoo Fibre overall, despite some positives.

To start with the good: when the connection actually works, the speeds are genuinely very good. Streaming, downloads, and general browsing are all fast and stable at times, which is what you’d hope for from a fibre provider.

However, the issues around everything else have really let it down.

Customer service has been a major pain point. It often feels like the support team doesn’t fully understand what’s being asked, even for relatively simple requests. On multiple occasions, I’ve tried to get straightforward changes made and it’s either taken far too long or hasn’t been done correctly at all.

A big limitation is the lack of control over the router. You can’t make basic network changes yourself — things like opening ports, changing the WiFi password, or even renaming your network. This is incredibly restrictive, especially if you have smart home devices, gaming setups, or anything that requires port forwarding or custom configuration. Most providers allow at least some level of user control, so this feels unnecessarily locked down.

I’ve also had ongoing issues with devices struggling to connect reliably. There have been multiple engineer visits, and while they’ve confirmed there is a problem, no one seems able to identify the root cause. To make matters worse, the engineers aren’t directly employed by Cuckoo, so there’s a bit of a disconnect in accountability and follow-up.

On the administrative side, things haven’t been much better. I submitted a subject access request over 2.5 months ago and am still waiting for a response, which is well beyond expected timeframes. Formal complaints also seem to disappear into a void — I’m told responses have been sent, but I’ve never actually received them.

In summary, while the raw internet speeds are strong, the lack of router control, poor customer support, unresolved technical issues, and slow (or nonexistent) responses to formal requests make this a difficult service to recommend.
