Avoid at all costs – Unprofessional and Dishonest

​I had some gold and silver to sell, so I decided to visit a few local dealers to get some quotes. I am incredibly glad I did my research beforehand, as this was easily one of the most dishonest and unprofessional business encounters I have ever had.

​From the moment we walked in, the attitude was poor. He became visibly frustrated when we refused to disclose the quotes we had already obtained from other dealers. Quite frankly, if you are an honest businessman, you shouldn't need to see someone else’s homework to give a fair market price.

​The experience only went downhill from there:

​Deceptive Practices: He insisted one of our items was fake, despite us knowing for a fact it was solid 14ct gold. Most shockingly, he then attempted to keep the item, including it in his "valuation" rather than handing it back, under the guise that it was worthless. ​

Undervaluing: He was adamant that an 18ct gold item was only 9ct. ​Lack of Expertise (or Integrity) We had a chain we thought was 9ct; he agreed, yet a subsequent honest company pointed out it was actually 15ct.

​The Bottom Line: I ended up being paid more than double his total quote by another dealer, and that was for less than half of the items he had appraised!

​When we wouldn't budge on revealing our other quotes, he snapped, saying something along the lines of, "If you don't want to sell, I’m not wasting my time looking!" We absolutely wanted to sell—we just wanted a fair price! This was before he had even valued the items we had.

​It deeply worries me that someone less prepared or unable to do their own research might walk into this shop and be completely taken advantage of. He is an unscrupulous man at the very least. Do yourself a favour and take your business elsewhere.

I have had the worst experience ever with this company. I would never recommend them to anyone again.

Around 10 years ago, I used this firm for another legal process with a lawyer called Thiago, who was extremely competent. Because of that positive experience, when I needed legal assistance again years later, they were the first company that came to mind.

I started a process with Isabella in February 2025 regarding wedding paperwork that needed to be completed before my wedding at the end of August. I was originally told that the entire process would take approximately four months and should have been finalised by June 2025 at the latest.

However, the process ended up taking over one year to be completed.

By June nothing was ready, and the same happened in July. The amount of stress that my partner and I went through was completely unnecessary, especially during what should have been a very happy period of our lives.

In the end, we had to get married without the proper ceremony because the documents were never completed on time.

After that, I spent months chasing updates through emails, phone calls, and WhatsApp messages, but Isabella — the lawyer I had signed the contract with — simply disappeared. She stopped replying to emails, messages, and calls.

When she finally decided to respond, she claimed that Brazilian law had changed and that the process would take longer. However, she never provided any proof, documentation, emails, or official evidence to support this explanation — only words.

October, November, and December passed with absolutely no updates from either Isabella or the company.

By January 2026, almost one year after starting the process, my partner and I decided to escalate the matter to HR because we genuinely felt we had been scammed and that the company had disappeared with our money. I had paid £4,000 upfront.

We then contacted the general email address listed on their website. A few days later, Martha from HR replied and said we would receive a solution within 14 days.

February 2026 marked exactly one year since the process had started, and after those 14 days passed, once again I heard nothing from anyone.

Eventually, I was passed to another lawyer whose name I cannot even remember.

By that point, my stress levels were beyond extreme. I felt exhausted, disappointed, angry, and genuinely shocked that this situation was still continuing after so long.

They asked me to come into the office for a meeting, but I refused because I did not want to go through the entire story again, especially considering how frustrated I already was.

Then, completely out of nowhere, one day I simply received all my documents at home — with no email, no explanation, no apology, and no communication whatsoever.

Conclusion: this company does not care about you, your process, your deadlines, or your personal life. The office is full of incompetent people who do not understand what proper client care means.

If you are thinking about starting a process with this company, please think twice — or even four times. I am sure there are far more professional and reputable firms out there.

I would never recommend this company or this experience to anyone ever again.

I contacted Compassion in Dying for guidance after being told by my mum’s GP surgery that a DNACPR decision was being arranged and “approved” with involvement from the ICB.

This immediately raised concerns, as this did not sound right. I contacted Compassion in Dying for advice and was extremely upset to be told, without any tact or sensitivity, that this information was correct.

I therefore contacted the ICB direct to question this.

Having since looked into this properly, I understand that DNACPR decisions are clinical decisions made by the treating doctor, with appropriate consultation with the patient and or their legal representative. They are not something that external bodies like the ICB approve.

I raised this with Compassion in Dying expecting accurate guidance and advice. Instead, I was told that the ICB can be involved in this way and that this is how the process works.

I have now received a formal written response from the ICB confirming the opposite.

They have clearly stated that:

1.	They have no involvement in individual DNACPR decisions

2.	They have had no contact with the GP regarding my mum

3.	They do not operate at that level

4.	There is no approval process through them and no documentation exists

This means the information I was given was incorrect.

This is not a minor issue. DNACPR decisions are serious, sensitive, and legally significant.

Families rely on organisations like this for accurate guidance, and in my case, incorrect information was reinforced rather than challenged.

For clarity, DNACPR decisions cannot be approved by the ICB. They must follow proper legal and clinical processes, including consultation and where applicable, involvement of the patient’s attorney under a Health and Welfare LPA.

For completeness, I have written confirmation from the ICB that they were not involved in my mum’s case, did not approve any DNACPR decision, and hold no related correspondence. This directly contradicts what I was told.

I would strongly advise others in a similar situation to verify information directly with the relevant authority and to challenge anything that does not sound right, rather than relying solely on third-party advice.

I always hate leaving negative reviews, but unfortunately I will have to on this occasion.

First and foremost, Analogue Wonderland as an analogue store is fantastic. I cannot fault them there- they have a great range of products at competitive prices and their customer service (in my experience so far) has been superb.

But I’ve had a few issues, however, with their film processing and scanning services.

The most recent example of this is when, not long ago, I sent in a roll of film (Lomography LomoChrome Colour ‘92 400) and recover scans that suggested this film was either expired (it wasn’t - expiry was 2027) or underexposed (something I out ruled immediately as the images looked over exposed lighting wise if anything, and the film was shot on a fairly bright day, metered on a rather pricy and trustworthy KEKS light meter). Despite this, I at first put the blame down to the film stock not being of adequate quality. I made a TikTok video about this, blaming the film stock as “unreliable”, only to be met with masses and masses of comments telling me that the problem is a scanning / lab problem- NOT film stock problem. Moreover, a lab/film scan technician commented and pulled a significant amount of more info to the image just from a screenshot of the TikTok video (pictured below). This, alongside two other more minor but similar scanning issues I’ve had with AW in the past, pretty much confirmed to me that their scanning technique is not consistent and needs improvement. I understand that AW offer a separate “professional editing” package (which I did not purchase with this order), but I truly expect better even at the baseline price.

Leaving this review on a positive note, I’d kindly ask for people to keep supporting Analogue Wonderland. Whilst I’ve obviously had issues with their scanning technique, they are honestly one of the driving forces reviving analogue photography in the Uk- businesses like these need our support!

On 7 January 2026, nearly three months after the group interview, I was finally invited to a 30-minute, one-to-one Zoom interview, which took place on 22 January. I was told I would hear back in two to three weeks.

It has now been over two months. I followed up on 26 January, 10 February, and 18 February. Not one of those emails received a reply.

We visited The River Garden yesterday at 2 pm after booking a table for six the day before. We travelled from Gerrards Cross expecting a pleasant experience and good customer service, but unfortunately the level of care and professionalism was extremely poor. It was very disappointing and will definitely be our first and last visit

Unfortunately, the overall service was poor and below what was advertised and expected.

Upon arrival, we were met with a very poor first impression. A member of staff at the entrance was on the phone and, despite clearly seeing us, made no effort to acknowledge or assist us. We were left to find our own way inside without any guidance or welcome, which was both unprofessional and discourteous.

After entering, we were greeted by a gentleman who appeared to be a manager and offered coffee or water. However, beyond this initial interaction, nothing is else was provided unless we repeatedly asked for it ourselves.

We were then assisted by a staff member who did our hair and was professional and pleasant. This was one of the few positive aspects of the experience.

However, several key services explicitly advertised in the brochure were not delivered:
•	The brochure states that clients should bring 4–6 outfits. I brought 6, yet we were told only 4 would be used. This is misleading and inconsistent with what was advertised.
•	The advertised aromatherapy hand massage was not offered or provided at any point.
•	The advertised skin preparation (including cleansing, toning, and moisturising with rose quartz stones and essential oils) was also not provided. When I asked about this, I was simply told “no” and makeup was applied without any preparation, to a very basic standard.

These omissions are unacceptable and constitute a clear failure to deliver the services promised. Another family present chose to leave upon realizing these services were not honored.

The photography session itself was acceptable, and the photographer was courteous. However, the experience deteriorated again during the photo viewing.

The same manager applied significant pressure on us to purchase additional photo packages. Despite clearly declining multiple times, he continued to push increasingly insistent offers, which made us feel extremely uncomfortable.

When I requested only our complimentary photos and the return of our £100 deposit, there was clear reluctance. After prolonged discussion, we were instead offered an additional photo in place of a refund, which we felt pressured into accepting.

The service we received did not match what was advertised, and the overall experience was disappointing, stressful, and at times, embarrassing.

I am trying now to request a refund of my deposit on the basis of:
•	Failure to provide advertised services
•	Misleading information in promotional materials
•	High-pressure sales tactics

However after reading other negative reviews here, I’m afraid they might not even get back to my message, as it looks like they have a tendency to ignore their customers after the service is “completed”.

Avoid yourself a headache and choose another place.

I genuinely regret trusting this company and I seriously question how they are operating as “professionals” in construction.

Before the work was even completed, I was relentlessly pressured through constant phone calls and WhatsApp messages to leave positive reviews. The contractor would repeatedly call me while I was out with family purely to ask me to write reviews for the company, despite the work not even being finished yet. Looking back now, the desperation for reviews before completing the work properly should have been the first major warning sign.

At the time, I trusted the company and agreed to leave a positive review — something I now completely regret.

The biggest issue throughout this entire experience was the constant refusal to listen to the client. I made it very clear from the beginning that I wanted the old flooring removed before the new flooring was installed, because I would later be replacing the skirting with another company. I raised concerns about this multiple times and was repeatedly dismissed and told there was “no need” and that it “wouldn’t be a problem.”

Instead, they laid the new flooring directly on top of the old flooring — clearly the quickest and laziest option possible.

When the skirting specialists later arrived, they immediately explained what any competent contractor should already know: the flooring should never have been installed this way if the skirting was going to be replaced, as it affects the levelling and risks damaging the new floor during installation. In other words, the exact issue I had repeatedly warned them about from the start.

The same thing happened in the kitchen. The walls clearly needed proper plastering, however the contractor again refused and insisted there was “no need.” Instead of carrying out the work properly, they simply painted over the existing issues because they clearly did not want to extend the job or put in the necessary effort. I specifically raised concerns about this beforehand and was again dismissed entirely. Now cracks are appearing throughout the kitchen walls exactly as I feared they would.

The most frustrating part was the dismissive attitude throughout the process. It genuinely felt as though my concerns were ignored because I was expected to know nothing about construction as a woman, despite the fact every concern I raised later turned out to be completely valid. Once deposits had been paid, I felt trapped into trusting their judgement, which was clearly a mistake.

The workmanship overall was careless and rushed. Certain flooring clips were glued down instead of properly fitted, corners and finishing were poorly executed, and the overall standard of work reflected a serious lack of professionalism and attention to detail.

To make matters worse, the workers repeatedly used our private bathroom throughout the day and consistently left it in a disgusting and unhygienic condition. The property was left messy, disrespected and badly managed overall.

This company appears far more focused on chasing reviews and rushing through jobs than actually delivering quality workmanship. I would strongly advise anyone considering using them to think very carefully before doing so. The stress, poor workmanship, dismissive attitude and complete disregard for client instructions made this one of the worst experiences I have had with any contractor.

If I could give 0 stars, I would.

Absolutely shocking experience with Sambo Tires.

My brother paid for a new tyre AND a weld repair on the alloy. We were clearly told by the worker that it would be “fine for a long time” — no mention whatsoever of “no guarantee” when they happily took the money.

I drove the car home (a short, careful drive), then went abroad. When I came back, the tyre was completely flat — clearly the repair failed almost immediately. That is nowhere near what any reasonable person would consider acceptable durability.

When I returned to sort it, instead of taking responsibility, the owner turned around and said ALL work has no guarantee. That’s not how a legitimate business operates. Under the Consumer Rights Act, services must be carried out with reasonable care and skill — and must last a reasonable amount of time. One drive home is a joke.

To make it worse, he started blaming my alloys, calling them “shit” — yet had no issue taking payment or assuring us the repair would last. Funny how the story changes after there’s a problem.

Then, after all that, they offered to “redo it” for £50 because they “have costs” — which just shows they KNOW the original job wasn’t done properly. If it was done right the first time, why would I need to pay again?

Also very convenient how every negative review gets brushed off with zero accountability — apparently they’re always perfect and never at fault.

Never go here. Avoid at all costs. Unprofessional, unreliable, and no accountability when things go wrong.

one_star_reviews.text:
ISCA states that it “promotes wellbeing.” This did not reflect our experience.

My daughter arrived in London happy, confident, and excited for her new experience, but she struggled to integrate because she was being excluded and bullied. Her wellbeing deteriorated quickly and significantly: she was stressed, had difficulty sleeping, lost weight, and was at times incapable even of attending lessons. After just four months, we felt we had no choice but to withdraw her from the school.

While some support was offered in line with the measures described on the school’s website, it was not effectively translated into practice. The focus appeared to be more on supporting the student being bullied rather than addressing the underlying causes of the bullying itself, and therefore did not lead to any meaningful improvement in the overall situation. Disappointingly, it is my daughter who has now lost out on the opportunity and experience of living and studying in London, rather than those who caused her suffering.

We were also mistakenly sent another student’s medical information, which raised serious concerns for us about data handling and protection. We subsequently submitted a data subject access request, and based on the information we received, it appeared to us that other students may also have been facing challenges.

Academically, the standard appeared acceptable. However, key information was not clearly communicated. Subjects such as English Literature and Mathematics were not provided, contrary to what we had understood. The additional preparatory year for St Martin’s, as well as the shorter school year (without the preparatory year), were also not made sufficiently transparent to us.

Despite her early withdrawal, the school was unwilling to offer even a partial refund, and we were left with the impression that responsibility was placed solely on us.

Since moving to a different school, my daughter is herself again. However, the emotional and financial impact remains.

This review is intended to share our personal experience and give other parents an impression of how situations like ours may be handled at this school. The school’s response, after everything that happened, speaks for itself. In our experience, this is the kind of support and communication parents can expect from ISCA.

one_star_reviews.text:
Buy British? Don't bother. A predatory and frustrating experience. Rating: 1 / 5

The UK Brand Myth: I paid a significant premium for these locks because I wanted to support a UK business and have the peace of mind of London-based support. It was a massive mistake. Simpled is a corporate facade operating out of a WeWork address, selling fragile hardware with a support system designed to stall and frustrate.

Pricing Chaos: There is zero consistency in their pricing. They list these locks at £169 on their website, sometimes discounted to £99, while charging £139 on Amazon. It is a blatant attempt to see how much they can squeeze out of you.

The Hardware Saga: I ordered three units initially. One arrived with a broken front panel. Despite the heavy price tag, this isn't some bespoke system. The locks run entirely on a basic, third-party app (TTLock). Worse yet, the core biometric feature is practically useless; the fingerprint sensor is so unreliable that the lock mostly wouldn't open even after 8 to 10 attempts. The replacement I eventually received for the broken unit appeared to be a used customer return and was just as defective.

The Most Ridiculous Part: When I had to replace another faulty component, the shipping took a full week. To make matters worse, they had the audacity to blame me for a part that broke while I was simply trying to fix their defective hardware. They then tried to charge me an extra £33 for the replacement part. I was only in that position because their original product was faulty, yet they tried to turn it into a profit-making opportunity.

The Support Nightmare: They boast about UK resident support, yet it routinely took them 24 hours or more to reply to a basic email. I spent a week in an exhausting loop of stalling tactics. Even after management admitted they got many things wrong, they suggested a resolution with an offer I didn't even ask for. Given the days of physical labor and the sheer administrative hassle they caused, the offer was quite frankly insulting anyway!

The Truth: I have since ripped these out and replaced them with alternative locks that cost only £40. To be honest, the £40 replacements are far superior in every way. The biometrics work instantly and the build quality puts Simpled to shame.

The Verdict: Save your money, your time, and your doors. You can buy a better product for £40 elsewhere and avoid the headache of a company that cares more about its image than its customers.

It is up to you to make your own mind up, but I have done the legwork so you don't have to.

UPDATE: The owner has replied below attempting to blame an "inexperienced team member." This is completely false. It was their Customer Service Manager who offered me an insulting token gesture after a week of stalling. Now they are suggesting I should have left a voicemail, despite them taking 24 plus hours to reply to basic emails.

Blaming your staff and even your customers instead of taking responsibility tells you everything you need to know about this company.

Title: £300 a year lost for being a loyal customer

As a long-standing customer with a substantial savings balance, I was very disappointed to discover I am receiving a significantly lower interest rate than what is currently offered to new customers on similar accounts.

This is not a small difference — it equates to hundreds of pounds per year in lost interest.

I raised this as a formal complaint, but the response did not explain why existing customers are left on lower rates or offer any meaningful solution. There is also no clear or proactive way to ensure customers are moved to more competitive rates.

I understand banks offer incentives to attract new customers, but this feels like a clear loyalty penalty. Existing customers should not be disadvantaged in this way.

Very disappointing experience.

I’m disappointed that Monument is offering 4.51% to new savers while existing long-term customers are left on a much lower rate of 3.77%.

That gap feels unfair, especially when you require a minimum balance of £25k, because the savings are substantial and the difference in interest really adds up over time.

I raised this concern and the reply was polite, but it did not properly address why loyal customers are left behind or offer a clear solution.

A bank that wants trust from savers should treat existing customers fairly as well as new ones.

No communication, no accountability, and no urgency when it matters most. Really disappointing experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
The original company is no longer in business.  A company with a similar name has been formed out of the ashes and creditors and clients of the original abandoned.  Just smoke and mirrors.

Cornflake Ltd (company number 06624584) entered Administration on 17 April 2026. Immediately thereafter the Administrator, Bretts Business Recovery, sold, by prior arrangement (in what is known as a “pre-packaged sale”), the IP, office furniture, etc, to a company called ADF Acquisition Co 1 Limited (“ADFA”, company number 17111369), which had been incorporated on 23 March 2026 explicitly for this purpose and whose shares are held indirectly by Groupe Ateliers de France (“GADF”).  Employee contracts were transitioned simultaneously.  ADFA appointed to its Board the MD of the original Cornflake entity (now a shell), and the Chief Administrative and Financial Officer at GADF, and then deftly changed its name on 21 April 2026 to Cornflake Group Ltd (“CGL”).

The above explanation contextualises the press statements made by GADF that it had acquired Cornflake.  It did not.  It had acquired (for a comparatively small consideration paid to Cornflake) selected assets out of that company and placed them, along with Cornflake’s employees, within a new company with a remarkably similar name, Cornflake Group Ltd.  GADF’s acquisition left various financial liabilities (and customer contracts – see below) in the original company for the Administrators to address as that entity inevitably transitions in due course to one in Liquidation.

Customer contracts that GADF and CGL evidently did not want, regardless of their significance to the clients and the impact on the properties / projects at which the automation systems contracted to Cornflake to develop were being implemented, were simply left behind in the original company, which now had no assets, resources or personnel, and so these incomplete projects were, in all respects, abandoned.  No warning of this action was provided to at least one such client whose repeated attempts, both personally and via the main contractor, to reach the Cornflake project team working on the contract in question were studiously ignored.  The now ex-client was simply provided with an electronic copy of the project file in its incomplete and un-commissioned state via the Administrators.  Even a message sent to the director of the new company asking if it would take on the completion of the virtually finished project went unanswered.  Yet, the relationship between this client and Cornflake’s team had always been cordial, collaborative and harmonious, with all Cornflake’s invoices paid promptly.

The MD of the original company, and now a director at the new “Cornflake” entity, is reported as stating that what has taken place “marks an important step forward for Cornflake…”.  That statement is at odds with the corporate reality: Cornflake Ltd has ceased trading, is now in administration (as reported on the file at Companies House) and will eventually go into liquidation.  Groupe Ateliers de France has simultaneously purchased some of Cornflake’s assets and parachuted them into a newco with a name which, to most observers, is much the same: “Cornflake Group” as opposed to “Cornflake”.

In sum, this is not, as is being trumpeted, an acquisition of a successful business but the cherry-picking of assets from within a company, Cornflake, that was presumably in serious financial trouble and has now been left in the shadows to be quietly buried.  Future customers of the successor entity, Cornflake Group Ltd, will want to take note of the fact that, if the director and team that have moved across from the now defunct company to the new one are willing to turn their backs on clients and simply cut them loose, without even offering transitional assistance on equitable commercial terms, they are just as likely to do it again should the new company itself suffer the same fate.  Once bitten, twice shy.

one_star_reviews.text:
Please Read Before Joining This Gym

My experience at this gym was extremely disappointing and far below the standard expected for the price being charged. The biggest issue, in my opinion, is management. They often give the impression that they are doing everything they can to help, but in reality very little seems to change. Problems continue, complaints appear to go nowhere, and it often feels like they simply do not care about genuine member concerns.

Another major issue is inconsistency in how rules are enforced. It can feel like some people are removed or treated harshly for unclear reasons, while other behaviour that should be addressed is ignored. In my experience, there were occasions where divisive conversations about politics and disrespectful comments about religions were tolerated without management taking meaningful action. A professional gym should make all members feel comfortable and respected regardless of their beliefs.

A large number of the staff seem inexperienced and unprofessional. Instead of creating a welcoming atmosphere, it often feels like there is too much gossip, unnecessary drama, and childish behaviour. Far too much of the environment comes across as rumours, back-and-forth stories, and “he said, she said” nonsense rather than a professionally run business focused on members.

The gym itself is frequently unclean, with machines often out of order and facilities not working as they should. For paying members, this becomes frustrating very quickly.

The spa area was especially poor. The sauna looks badly maintained, with old wood that appears to be patched up rather than properly replaced. The steam room often had an unpleasant smell and did not feel clean. The pool at times appeared unclean and overly chlorinated. The jacuzzi was often not warm enough, and the cold plunge area looked unhygienic and in need of serious upkeep.

Most importantly, the membership cost does not reflect the quality provided. For similar prices, gyms such as David Lloyd or Virgin Active offer a much better standard of cleanliness, maintenance, and customer service. There, you feel like you get what you pay for.

Overall, this place felt more like a poorly managed social club than a premium gym. I would strongly recommend people look elsewhere before committing.

As a member of over three years, I feel it’s important to share my honest experience.

Throughout my time at the club, I have consistently respected policies, conducted myself professionally, and contributed positively to the environment. I have also referred approximately 10–50 new members and, on multiple occasions, stepped in during incidents to help maintain a safe and respectful atmosphere.

Despite this, I was recently accused of something I categorically deny. I made this clear, yet I was told there were “witnesses,” which is simply not true. While I understand the club’s right to make decisions, I cannot ignore how unfair and, at times, discriminatory this situation has felt—especially considering I have witnessed more serious incidents involving other members who were still welcomed back.

Financially, my membership started at £97 per month and increased steadily over time to £137. Despite this, the facilities have frequently fallen below standard. There have been repeated issues such as the sauna, steam room, and jacuzzi not functioning properly, and equipment like the Smith machine being out of service for extended periods—sometimes for an entire month at a time. While the equipment itself is decent, it is noticeably outdated and not consistently maintained.

I remained patient and loyal, hoping for improvements, but unfortunately, that has not been the case.

I respect the club’s final decision, even if I strongly disagree with the basis of it. However, I would advise potential members to carefully consider both the service quality and how long-term members are treated.

I wish the business all the best moving forward and hope to see improvements in both facilities and member relations. As for myself, I will be taking my membership elsewhere.

I do not believe it is professional, fair, or appropriate for your company to encourage or instruct staff members who work at your facilities to leave positive reviews about the club. Reviews are intended to reflect the genuine experiences of members and visitors, not biased opinions influenced by management. When employees are asked to contribute favourable feedback, it undermines the credibility and trustworthiness of those reviews. I have also included a screenshot showing staff members posting positive reviews, as I feel this practice is misleading and should not be taking place. Overall, this approach appears unprofessional and raises concerns about how much the organisation truly values honest feedback from its members.

Overall a waste of time and money.

This facility is not worth the time or cost. The premises are poorly maintained, with unpleasant odors and outdated equipment. Key amenities, including the sauna and steam room, are frequently out of order. Staff are unprofessional, and there is a clear lack of customer care. There have also been ongoing concerns about vehicle damage in the car park, with little to no response from management.

After more than five years as a member, there has been no meaningful improvement. Recent additions, such as the ice tub, appear unsuitable for commercial use and lack proper filtration. Overall, the service provided does not reflect the fees charged. I would strongly advise against signing up if you are looking for a reliable and well-managed fitness facility. Just signed up for David Lloyd’s and it’s 20 times better lol.

Furthermore, staff members should not be advised to leave reviews based on facilities they work in as is biased not appropriate for a company to ask its own staff members to leave reviews. I’ve noticed that individuals such as Klaudia and Lauren, who appear to be employees, have submitted reviews. As a business, encouraging internal staff to post reviews undermines trust and comes across as unprofessional. Customer feedback should be genuine and independent.

I wouldn’t recommend this spa to anyone after the experience I had.

From the moment I arrived, the atmosphere felt off. The receptionist was unprofessional and came across as inexperienced, giving dirty looks and showing no basic customer service. It felt uncomfortable straight away, like I wasn’t welcome there at all.

Things escalated when I was wrongly accused of using my phone by the poolside, which I hadn’t been doing. Instead of addressing it respectfully, they handled it in a rude and confrontational way, which made the situation embarrassing for no reason.

The pricing also made no sense. I’ve been before and paid £15 for a day pass, but this time I was told it was £20. What made it worse is that my friend went on the exact same day and paid £15 without any issues. There was no explanation for the difference, which just makes it feel unfair and inconsistent.

To top it all off, the cleanliness was unacceptable. The showers were dirty and clearly not maintained properly. Even worse, there was actual poo on the floor in the changing area, which is completely disgusting and shouldn’t happen in any spa environment.

Overall, the whole place felt poorly managed, unhygienic, and unprofessional. Between the rude staff, false accusations, inconsistent pricing, and lack of basic cleanliness, it’s definitely not somewhere I’ll be going back to. I’d strongly advise others to avoid it.

I had a very disappointing experience with the membership process. I was initially quoted a fee of £136, which I agreed to and signed a contract for. However, just three days later, I received a call stating there had been a “processing error” and that the actual cost would be £146.

What made the situation worse was the way it was handled. I was told, quite bluntly, that I had to either accept the higher fee or leave—despite the mistake being entirely on the club’s side which was incredibly unprofessional.

Had I been quoted £146 from the start, I would have had no issue paying it, but given that a contract had already been agreed and signed at £136, I expected the club to honour that agreement rather than put me in a position where I felt pressured to accept a higher price or walk away.

Overall, a very frustrating experience and not the level of service I would expect from a club claiming to be "luxury".

one_star_reviews.text: I contemplated whether I would write a poor review or just run and never look back - but I want to warn other pet owners of the lack of competency this company has as I would have wanted to have known. We had booked with PetAir months in advance to fly our dog from the UK to NZ. When the war in the UAE broke out and we were three weeks out from our departure I assumed everything was still all fine as I hadn’t heard a single thing from PetAir. I reached out to Emma a week later just in case, to check everything was ok and at that point only after I made contact, she said that Emirates were no longer transporting animals through Dubai (!!) I did panic but after a very emotional phone call wondering what the hell I was going to do, she promised me that she would be in contact with alternative options over the following days - but at this point there was no other option (we were also leaving the UK at the same time and had no one to care for our dog post our departure). I patiently waited and waited for her to reach me over the coming days with an update but to no avail. When I finally emailed her for an update (10 days out from departure) she had her out of office on and had gone off on annual leave!! We felt totally left in the lurch and had no support from PetAir. At this point I desperately contacted other animal transport agencies to ask about options they had (despite having over £1500 deposit tied up with PetAir) which they all confidently told me they could absolutely send our dog through the US, although it would be more expensive. PetAir had nothing to offer us in terms of options yet all the other transport agents I spoke with had flights lined up to be booked the morning I called them!! I had to push and push PetAir to pursue the USA route as we were getting desperate and I didn’t want to lose my £1500 deposit. At the last minute Emirates put all their flights back on so fortunately we still sent him through the Middle East, but to top it all off the caretag tracker (that we paid extra for) was supposed to give us updates while he travelled but never gave us a single update apart from the drop off at Heathrow! Waste of money, and although I was eventually refunded this cost, I had to work hard for it. Will never ever use them again and would never recommend them! Beware!

Due to their negligence we never had heating for 6 months during winter in our flat, nor the pin code or access to sign in to the app despite repeated requests, and in the end they charged us 1,700 pounds for unpaid heating and hot water bills WHICH WE NEVER HAD ACCESS TO IN THE FIRST PLACE. This is just 1 of many things, we had constant blockages in the shower and sinks in both bathrooms, to which they would send a contractor 2 weeks after initial contact, and when the problem would continuously reoccur, they stopped sending contractors to fix it and tried to charge us a further 900 pounds in rent deductions, until we proved their negligence via an email chain they left as proof. Complete Prime Residential Ltd has managed several properties for me for a number of years and the experience has been thoroughly unsatisfactory and frustrating.
On their website, CPRL claim to deliver "superior results, through innovation, expertise and unwavering client focus".  Yet the reality is that they frequently fail to respond to emails, and on the occasions when I have tried to call them, nobody answered the  phone. CPRL's Shaun Malston promised me in 2024 that the problems with CPRL's non-response to emails would be fixed, but this has not been done.
CPRL claim that they "don't just manage properties, [they] optimize them for maximum yield and minimum hassle". The rent  review at my property is overdue, and I asked CPRL two months ago to advise the market rent for the property, however they have failed to reply despite reminders sent to Shaun Malston (as the property manager also failed to reply). They can't even confirm who is living in the property. Trying to deal with CPRL has consistently been a major hassle.
CPRL claims that their "leadership team" provides day to day management with "professional rigor" (sic) but again, this is not my experience. For example, CPRL allowed the tenants at my property to make deductions from the rent to cover some expenditure without asking me or informing me. They then concealed the expenditure by not including it in the rent statements, which instead showed arrears by the tenants. After I queried this with CPRL, it took them more than six months and at least 10 emails, including following up on  emails unanswered by CPRL, before they eventually addressed it. Shaun Malston's claim that the "mistake" was quickly addressed when identified is untrue. Certainly there was no "professional rigor" by CPRL, who provided inaccurate rent statements for over a year and they would have continued to do this if I had not raised the matter with them.
CPRL's  claims that they stand out by delivering  "superior results through innovation, expertise and unwavering client focus" are not consistent with my experience. On the contrary, the results provided by CPRL are substandard and unsatisfactory. Their repeated failure to respond to emails has wasted so much time and caused so much frustration.
CPRL claims to "handle every issue with precision and care", but this is also untrue. For example, I have been out of pocket for over a year by more than GBP 1,000 in admin and legal fees I had to pay due to CPRL's failure to settle the ground rent for my property, despite the freeholder having sent multiple reminders to them. As a result, the freeholder threatened to forfeit my lease and I risked losing my property. After I complained, Shaun Malston only provided incoherent comments about bounceback messages. In any event, it is obvious that CPRL failed to handle the situation competently or professionally. There was no care or precision by CPRL at all. They couldn't care less.
Although CPRL claims to have a complaints handling process, all you can expect from it are obfuscation and evasion.
Based on my experience, anyone looking for a lettings and management agent should avoid this inefficient company.

I am extremely upset and deeply concerned about the conditions on 6D, where my father is currently recovering from emergency open heart surgery and awaiting another procedure. The conditions patients are being forced to endure are completely unacceptable and inappropriate for a hospital environment.
The air conditioning on the unit is not working, leaving patients, families, and staff dealing with unbearable heat. Patients are not allowed to use fans or open windows, resulting in little to no ventilation or relief in the rooms. For individuals recovering these conditions are not only uncomfortable but potentially dangerous.
Since being in these conditions, my father has developed a persistent cough that continues to worsen. I strongly believe the excessive heat and poor airflow are negatively affecting his recovery. Patients recovering  should be healing in a safe, clean, and temperature controlled environment not in conditions that place additional stress on their bodies and compromise their recovery.
What is even more concerning is that these conditions increase the risk of serious health complications, including dehydration, respiratory distress, heat exhaustion, and even heatstroke for vulnerable patients. In a hospital setting, poor ventilation and excessive heat can also create concerns regarding sanitation, infection control, and the spread of illness. Patients recovering from surgeries are already medically fragile and should not be exposed to conditions that could increase the risk of infection or other preventable complications.
This issue is affecting more than just my father. Other patients, visitors, and even staff members are visibly struggling with the heat. It is honestly shocking and incredibly disappointing that this situation has been allowed to continue without urgent action being taken.
A hospital should prioritize patient safety, comfort, sanitation, and proper healing conditions at all times. Unfortunately, the current environment on 6D does not reflect those standards. While I understand maintenance problems can happen, the lack of urgency in resolving this issue is unacceptable considering the of the patients being cared for on this unit.

I had several episodes of superficial thrombosis over several years and in December 2025, I was admitted to Southend Hospital, Essex with double embolisms. A PET scan showed a 13mm nodule that was next to blood vessels but the lymph nodes were  clear of cancer.   I was advised that to remove the nodule, it had to be done at St Barts via the RATS (robotic arm) procedure. I kept chasing up the appointment and ended up with waiting 10 weeks for a biopsy.

The consultant appeared to be very professional and had great experience with robotics in the medical field and completed the first microwave ablation technique in the UK.   I had noted on his profile after the operation, that if I was paying privately that  an appointment would have been much sooner.

I also waited 4 weeks for the results and was devasted to learn that it is stage 3 lung cancer! The consultant had offered a phone consultation but with hind sight, I should have seen him face to face as it was difficult to hear.

I assumed after the long wait, he would have taken a whole lobe out but he only took a segment out.   By then it was a highly aggressive BRAF mutation on the liwer lobe, it had  invaded 3 nodes, blood vessels, air spaces and the margin was not clear!  All putting me at a massive risk of reoccurence!

After several weeks and waiting for both hospitals MDT (Multidisciplinary Team Meeting) and no further treatment yet, St Barts has said they now believe the margin was clear.  That still does not help the invasion that has reached the middle sternum and invasion of the other areas. I am very upset and dissappointed to hear all of this. The prognosis is awful, despite them talking about better treatments!  I feel robbed of my life now due to incompetence.and lack of care!
I will never be happy knowing the cancer is circulating my body. 6 months and still no treatment.

Don't be fobbed off by these  hospitals not screening you for cancer when you have repeated episides of blood clots.   20% of people with cancer has blood clots.  Don't allow them to make you wait for an urgent biopsy. Don't think you get better care in a London Hospital.  I found out the other day that the tumour removal could have been done locally via VATS (video robotics) but the Southend consultant never told me this as I thought it would have to have been open surgery.

one_star_reviews.text:
I purchased a Tesla Model S from M&W Automotive through a business purchase and, unfortunately, my experience after the sale has been disappointing.

To be fair, I am happy with the car overall. However, there were two significant issues with the vehicle, and the main problem has been how those issues were handled after the sale.

I travelled from the north and spent most of the day getting there, with delays along the way, which is why I arrived later than planned. I had originally intended to arrive around 2pm to allow sufficient time for inspection. When I arrived at around 4pm, with the dealership closing at 5pm, I asked how much time I had to inspect the vehicle and was told 10 minutes. I requested 25 minutes, which was agreed, but this is still not enough time to properly inspect a car, especially an electric vehicle. I relied heavily on the dealership’s reviews and the advertised three month guarantee.

The vehicle was advertised as coming with a three month guarantee as standard, with options to extend this further. Based on the wording, this gave the impression of a manufacturer-level warranty included in the price. I declined the paid 12 month warranty on that basis, believing I had three months of cover if any issues arose. However, when issues were raised, no written terms or scope of this guarantee were provided.

Shortly after purchase, I identified that the top DRLs in both front headlights were not working and reported this almost immediately. I was told they were working at collection, which does not align with my experience. A Tesla inspection later confirmed that all front suspension arms and one rear arm were worn to the point where wheel alignment could not be carried out after approximately 1,500 miles, which Tesla indicated is not consistent with such wear developing over that distance.

To keep things reasonable, I avoided Tesla’s repair route, which would have cost several thousand pounds. Instead, I sourced a specialist to repair the DRLs for around £250 and purchased the suspension arms myself for around £270, covering installation separately. I asked only for a contribution towards these parts (around £520), but this was not responded to.

It is worth noting that a fault with the boot actuator was disclosed at the point of sale and they did contribute £120 towards that repair, which I appreciate. However, more significant undisclosed issues were not treated in the same way.

I rarely leave negative reviews and, as a business owner myself, I try to support other businesses. This is a genuine account of my experience. Many customers may have a good experience if no issues arise, but in my case the after-sales support was lacking.

I did try to resolve the situation fairly and gave the dealership an opportunity to address it before leaving this review, but unfortunately that was not taken.

Based on my experience, I would encourage others to take their time and ensure any warranty or guarantee is clearly defined in writing before purchasing.

After three experiences with this salon, I feel it’s fair to share my experience honestly.

I’ve actually had genuinely positive experiences here previously, particularly with Maleeha and El (who has now left), which makes this more disappointing to write. However, I’ve increasingly found the management style and pricing approach difficult to reconcile with the experience being delivered.

This most recent visit was a 15-minute child’s haircut by Mikaela costing £25 under the salon’s “pay by time” model. My son sat calmly and completely still throughout.

I’ll let the photos (taken on the day of the cut) speak for themselves.

For me, the result didn’t align with the premium standard the salon presents online. The blend appears uneven in places, the neckline looks unfinished, the sideburns are uneven, and there are patches where the hair appears noticeably shorter than others, leaving visible lines. Overall, the cut lacked the level of refinement and attention to detail I would expect from a salon positioning itself as specialist-led and high-end.

What also sits uncomfortably with me is that this isn’t the first time the pricing structure has felt difficult to justify. On a previous occasion, when my son was frightened of haircuts, El very kindly spent around 10 minutes trying to settle him. Unfortunately the haircut wasn’t successful and not a single hair was cut, yet I was still asked to pay £18. This was despite the salon being empty at the time; staff were sweeping outside and I had only popped in on the off chance, so no appointment slot had been lost. I did explain that his hair hadn’t been touched and the management ultimately waived the fee.

During the period where my son struggled with haircuts, we visited several salons who invested time and patience into helping him feel comfortable. Many of them either charged very little or nothing at all when a haircut could not actually be completed. In many of those cases, I still chose to make a payment out of appreciation for the time and care shown.

I fully appreciate that people’s time has value, and I have no issue paying premium prices for premium service and results. But for me, there seems to be a disconnect between the salon’s branding, pricing and the overall customer experience being delivered.

If you're interested in the sixth form here please carefully consider your decision. I wouldn't want anyone to make the same mistakes we did with our son.
It markets itself as an inclusive music school and it really is. It bends over backwards to accommodate anyone with an issue of some sort. The problem is, if you don't have additional needs or you're not part of an underrepresented group, you're encouraged to let others have their own way. (It's unkind not to.)
But it's a miserable existence when you have no say in anything because a fellow 17 or 18-year old might cry if they can't choose the song you perform in your group, for example. I am not making that up - one student did cry because she was outvoted in her group and the tutor expected everyone else to cave in. It can be quite a manipulative environment in that sense, democracy doesn't really work. Everyone is entitled - but of course, someone has to bend.
If you're a boy, or a girl who doesn't have additional needs, it will be you and that pattern will be set.
My youngest child has SEND so I have no axe to grind on that front. Our approach has always been to work with the school to help him to do the work everyone else does and he's flying.
At the RS the preferred route seems to be exemptions. Some people miss certain lessons. They get given extensions constantly. They farm out the bits they can't do to others who can - great, they get the grade but what are they actually learning? The tutors know - one even made a joke about it in my son's class, asking 'are you actually going to do your own work today'?

Other students have already started to build music careers outside the RS are let off too. You have to perform on the other side of the world? That's okay, you go off when your coursework is due, don't worry. Then they wonder why nobody turns up during marked assessments.
If you just want to work hard and get on with things it's probably going to be tough for you here because your needs will most likely be low down in the pecking order. Rules don't seem to apply to everyone - but they probably will to you.
I have raised all this with the leadership and their response is that everyone has their own path to follow. It's what they tend to hide behind whenever you question them.
The great thing about it is they do give students a platform to perform and the time to work on their music skills. But they don't really show you how to do anything. You are just told what to do and you have to find a way through.
What my son has learned here is resilience, which is perhaps the greatest gift the RS could have given him. It is a tough old world out there - he's prepared for that now.

one_star_reviews.text:
I was referred to this dentist by Smile White for my Invisalign treatment, and from my very first appointment, I found the dentist’s manner to be blunt and lacking in clear communication. As someone without professional dental knowledge, I expected procedures, terminology, and aftercare to be explained clearly rather than feeling dismissed when asking questions.

While this was initially frustrating, my most recent experiences have been far more concerning. For my first bond removal appointment, I was specifically asked over the phone to bring my retainers with me. However, during the appointment, the dentist made no mention of them, did not check the fit, and did not advise me to put them on. I had to raise this myself just before leaving. Similarly, I was told I would be shown how to properly use my whitening kit, yet this was also overlooked entirely without explanation or guidance.

Additionally, my appointment was scheduled for 12:00 during my lunch break, yet I was not seen until approximately 12:40. This significant delay, without any prior warning or communication, was highly inconvenient and unprofessional.

Once seen, the treatment itself felt rushed and incomplete. I had to return multiple times during the same appointment because bond residue was repeatedly missed. After being strongly encouraged to see a hygienist, I attended my own hygienist (separate dentist practice) two days later, only to be informed that further bond material had still been left on my teeth.

When I returned to have this corrected, I was extremely disappointed by the dentist’s dismissive and unprofessional attitude. Comments such as “I’ve never had issues like this before,” “well I can’t see it,” and “you’re seeing things” were inappropriate and made me feel as though my concerns were not being taken seriously. Rather than carrying out a thorough professional check, I was expected to identify and point out the remaining bond material myself.

Given the significant financial investment involved in this treatment, this level of care is unacceptable. Having to repeatedly return, identify missed bond residue myself, and chase basic aftercare information was incredibly frustrating and left me feeling undervalued as a patient. While the reception staff and dental assistants were consistently polite, helpful, and professional, this does not excuse the poor clinical care I received.

Overall, I am deeply disappointed by the lack of professionalism, communication, thoroughness, and patient care demonstrated by the dentist. What should have been a straightforward final stage of treatment became unnecessarily stressful, time-consuming, and upsetting.

EDIT response to reply from practice:

Thank you for your response.

I would like to clarify that my treatment did not involve “multiple” consistently thorough reviews over six months as suggested. I attended approximately 3–4 appointments during this period, with several appointments also running late by around 15 minutes, not just one occasion.

Most concerning is that issues I raised regarding remaining composite were initially overlooked, and on more than one visit, material was only acknowledged after I specifically pointed it out, with the dentist stating words to the effect of “oh yes, I do see it now.” This directly contradicts the suggestion that all concerns were comprehensively identified and addressed at each stage.

My review reflects my personal experience of inconsistent attention to detail, delays, and communication that often left me feeling dismissed rather than reassured. While I appreciate your acknowledgment of communication concerns, I do not feel your response fully reflects the reality of my experience or adequately addresses the substance of my concerns.

I believe patient feedback should be responded to transparently and accurately, rather than with statements that minimise legitimate concerns.

Dishonest and patronising experience.
The first red flag is when you call to book and they ask, “Have you been here before?” It becomes obvious this is to decide how to handle you. If you’re a returning customer, the tone becomes even more patronising; if you’re new, they sound like they can barely be bothered until they figure out whether the job is “worth their while.”

I was charged just under £350 for a VW service. I told them the price was excessive, and the response was dismissive and condescending. I was told they “use original parts” and that I should have said if I didn’t want them. Then came the excuse that “oil prices have gone up because of conflict.” The tone and speed of the explanation felt like a tactic to make you second‑guess yourself. Many other reviewers have mentioned the same behaviour. Parts and oil haven’t suddenly become gold.

To check, I contacted VW Slough for a written quote for the exact same service:
Service & Inspection with extended scope: £270 — all original parts, VAT, and labour included.
This garage, however, adds VAT on top of everything, which is exactly what many people are calling out as a scam.

They also tried to sell me a yearly plan for far less than what they charged me today. On top of that, the person serving me even used religion — because we share the same one — to try to win me over. Completely inappropriate.

To make matters worse, they spilled oil on internal components. Once the engine warmed up, oil vapour filled the cabin. That tells you everything about the rushed, careless workmanship.

I can afford the loss, but others shouldn’t have to go through this. There are main dealers and independent garages that actually value customers, listen to what you want, and build trust. Unfortunately, you won’t find that here. I’d strongly recommend going elsewhere if you want transparency, respect, and proper value for your money.

Thanks for your patronising response, you know you’re in the wrong, don’t make it out like you told me all the fine print. Anyone would be stupid enough to come back to you, to correct anything.  Thanks for also mentioning my previous 1 star reviews, it was nothing to do you and were legitimate complaints. The basement food section at Japan Centre Flagship Store is, bluntly, an embarrassment. The yakitori arrived cold, which is already unacceptable, but what followed made it worse. It was clearly microwaved. Not reheated properly, not finished on a grill, just shoved in a microwave and sent back out. The result was grim.

The grilled eel had the texture and elasticity of rubber. Chewy, limp, and deeply unpleasant.

The sashimi didn’t redeem anything. Poorly cut, uneven, and in some pieces not even sliced all the way through, it looked careless and tasted just as uninspired. There’s a level of precision and respect that defines Japanese cuisine, and this felt like the complete abandonment of both. It came across as “close enough is good enough,” which is the last philosophy you’d ever associate with Japan at its best.

And then there’s the pricing. Charging three times what you’d expect to pay for food of this quality anywhere else in the world is not just unjustified, it’s borderline insulting. High prices can be acceptable when they come with quality, care, and execution. None of that is present here.

What you’re left with is overpriced, poorly prepared, and fundamentally disrespectful food that trades on the reputation of a cuisine it fails to honour. Avoid it.

Under clause 19(b)(i), our liability ceases when your property is collected from storage by you or your agent. I’ve had one or two poor customer service experiences in my life, but my weeks-long struggle with Vodafone has left me so demoralised that today after speaking with them for the umpteenth time I announced to my family I was going to bed.
I hold Lasting Power of Attorney for an elderly man aged 98. He had no need for most of the services he had on contract with them, so I cancelled them, with great difficulty. When that side of things finally appeared to be resolved, I requested a pay-as-you-go service for my friend, carefully explaining before proceeding that I would be operating the account. I provided all of my LPA documents, my email and mobile number, and awaited details of the new service that they promised to send via email.
Nothing.
Then commenced another almighty struggle to convince them to allow me to operate the new service, which in law, I am entitled to do. Even after patiently explaining the situation all over again and drawing their attention to the legal documents provided, they would not allow me to access nor operate the new service.
I have had no problems administering my friend’s bank account, commissioning his care from the council, placing his property on the market, etc., as his Lasting Power of Attorney.
The only organisation that simply will not support this elderly gentleman appropriately is Vodafone.
This nightmare odyssey is absolutely worthy of a complaint to Ofcom, if I can stomach it. At this point I genuinely believe I am suffering from C-PTSD as a result of the treatment I have been subjected to by Vodafone, who have passed the buck, stonewalled, lied and gaslit me over the course of multiple calls and emails totalling eight to ten hours over the course of the past four to six weeks.
Avoid Vodafone at all costs.

Review of Vodafone UK

I have just spent over an hour trying to complete a basic account function—changing my eSIM—and it has been an exercise in complete systemic failure.

The chatbot “TOBi” does not provide support; it actively blocks access to it

Calling 191 leads to long, irrelevant menu loops with no meaningful outcome

The system promises an SMS, then disconnects without resolving anything

On repeat attempts, voice input is ignored, keypad-only is forced, and calls are terminated

Critically, the online contact/complaints page is not even functional, removing yet another route to support

At this point, there is no effective way to contact Vodafone to manage my account.

This raises serious legal concerns.

Under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, services must be delivered with reasonable care and skill. A telecom provider that makes it impossible for customers to access support—particularly for essential account functions—is arguably failing to meet that obligation.

Further, Ofcom requires telecom providers to maintain accessible and effective complaint handling procedures. A system that traps customers in automated loops, disconnects calls, and provides no working contact channels cannot reasonably be described as accessible or effective.

This is not poor service—it is structural avoidance of customer contact.

If customers cannot communicate with their provider, then the service itself is fundamentally compromised. At that point, the question becomes unavoidable: is this a breach of contract?

Customers should seriously consider whether they are receiving the service they are paying for. If enough people begin cancelling contracts on the basis that support is inaccessible, perhaps standards will improve.

As it stands, this experience is unacceptable and falls far below what should be expected from a major UK telecommunications provider.

Over two years ago, this pharmacy seriously mishandled my controlled medication prescription, and to this day I still consider it one of the most stressful and disturbing experiences I have ever had with a healthcare provider.

I was repeatedly told that all of my medication had already been dispensed, despite the fact that my GP could clearly see on the system that there were still outstanding prescriptions remaining. My GP contacted the pharmacy regarding the discrepancy, and even specialists from the pain clinic attempted to clarify the situation with them. Despite this, the pharmacy continued insisting that everything had already been collected and refused to properly resolve the issue.

This involved controlled medication — not vitamins, not over-the-counter tablets, but medication that is strictly monitored and recorded. Mistakes involving controlled substances are extremely serious and can have major consequences for patients. The fact that multiple medical professionals could see one thing on the system while the pharmacy claimed the complete opposite remains deeply concerning to me.

What made the situation even worse was the attitude afterwards. Instead of acknowledging the possibility of an error and handling the matter professionally, I was labelled “rude” simply for questioning obvious inconsistencies and advocating for myself based on evidence from my GP and pain clinic consultant.

Now, years later, I am still being treated differently and refused services because I challenged their mistake instead of staying silent. Holding a grudge against a patient for raising legitimate concerns about controlled medication is completely unacceptable and profoundly unprofessional.

Patients deserve transparency, accountability, and safe handling of prescriptions — especially controlled substances. Based on my experience, I would strongly advise others to carefully monitor every prescription and double-check everything themselves when dealing with this pharmacy.

If you’ve ever wondered what society might look like after civilisation collapses, this country park offers a disturbingly accurate preview. The ground is carpeted — truly carpeted — with dog poo, as if the earth itself has given up and decided to wear a permanent brown polka‑dot pattern.

The dogs roam freely, naturally. Leads are apparently relics of a bygone era, like manners or basic human decency. Every few minutes, a new canine projectile launches itself at you, barking like it’s auditioning for a horror film. And the owners? They hover nearby, watching proudly, as though their dog’s behaviour is some kind of Olympic sport.

Try to speak up and you’ll unlock the park’s bonus level: a barrage of aggression from middle‑aged and older women who transform instantly into professional insult‑throwers. It’s like being shouted at by a chorus of furious aunties who’ve decided you’re the villain in their personal soap opera.

Bring children only if you want them to experience:

the thrill of dodging unpredictable animals

the joy of stepping in something warm

and the educational value of hearing language that would make a sailor blush

It’s less “country park” and more “post‑apocalyptic training ground,” but hey — at least it’s consistent.

These concerns were reported early, and both Stratstone Customer Services and Audi UK were notified. After my second visit, I was quoted to fix some of the issues, which I refused as the vehicle had been supplied in that condition. I was then advised that this would be resolved internally and that I would be contacted the following day. This did not happen, and after several days without contact, I had to escalate the matter through Stratstone and Audi UK. Even after multiple emails, there was still a delay before Milton Keynes Audi eventually made contact to arrange further work.

The vehicle was then booked in for several days. During this visit, adaptations were carried out, the AWD system oil was flushed, and the gearbox sump plug leak was addressed for a second time.

Over the 5.5 months, the vehicle was returned multiple times — five visits in total — for inspection and repair. During this time, further work was carried out, including additional adaptations and eventually a major gearbox repair with full dual clutch and associated component replacement and another awd oil flush as the judder and rummlbe returned just after 1500miles,

Despite this significant work, the original fault remained completely unresolved, and the vehicle continued to behave in the same way.

I returned the car again, and while the issue was acknowledged, I was advised that further investigation would depend on comparing the vehicle with another similar car, with no clear resolution path or timeline provided. At this stage, after multiple visits, extensive time invested, and no improvement, the situation became unreasonable.

Following the major repair, I obtained an independent gearbox and drivetrain specialist report prior to my final visit to Milton Keynes Audi, which included video evidence and highlighted multiple concerns that should have been identified during the dealership’s own diagnostic process.

Communication throughout was inconsistent, unclear, and difficult to follow, often requiring repeated follow-ups and leaving me without clear answers. This added unnecessary stress to what was already a prolonged and frustrating experience.

It is important to note that I made a conscious effort to allow multiple repair attempts rather than rejecting the vehicle early, in good faith, hoping the issue would be resolved. However, after such extensive work and no improvement, confidence in both the vehicle and the process was lost.

The vehicle was ultimately rejected through my finance provider due to the unresolved faults,who reviewed the evidence and handled the matter professionally.

While some staff were polite and did acknowledge the issue, the overall experience — particularly the lack of effective diagnosis, failure to resolve a serious fault, and poor communication — fell well below expectations for a premium brand.

Visited Waterfront Cafe Benson recently and left very disappointed.

The pricing lacks transparency. For example, scrambled eggs are charged extra as it’s more effort , but this isn’t mentioned anywhere. Being told to pay more at the till for something that isn’t clearly listed feels misleading.

What’s more frustrating is the constant messaging about “supporting local businesses.” Customers do want to support local—but not when they feel taken advantage of. In this case, a £2 surprise charge ended up costing them far more in lost business. We have happily spent more overall previously at this joint itself, but the new managers greed is beyond baffling.  Experiences like this make it hard to return.

Service and overall management also seem to have declined, which is a real shame as this used to be a dependable spot.

I hope the management rethinks their approach—clear pricing and fair treatment go a long way in keeping  loyal customers.
Reservations not required
